passages.name: celestia
passages.source_raw:
Celestia is a vibrant and lively planet, known for its incredible nightlife and endless parties. The planet is a paradise for those who love to dance and have a good time, with clubs and bars open late into the night and a constant stream of live music and entertainment.
My aunt and uncle have lived on Celestia for as long as I can remember, and they absolutely love it. Even though they don't work in the nightlife industry, they are always out and about, enjoying the music and the atmosphere. They have made a lot of friends on the planet, and they always seem to be having a great time, no matter what they are doing.

passages.name: intro2
passages.source_raw:
<<narrator>>You get up to answer the doorbell, and find //<<link 'Damon'>><<popup 'damon' 'Database'>><</link>>// standing on your porch, looking anxious and rushed.

<<speech "damon" "Damon">>Hey, $name. Sorry to show up unannounced like this, but I have some important news. The authorities are looking for your dad and they have orders to arrest you, your $mom, and your $sis. You have to leave the planet now. I have a ship at the hangar, we have to go there as soon as possible. Can you be ready to go in the next 10 minutes?<</speech>>

You are shocked by Damon's news and struggle to process what he is saying. You turn to your $mom and $sis, who are equally stunned.

<<speech $you "$name">>What is this? Where is dad? Why are they looking for him?<</speech>>

<<speech $c_mom "$name_mom">>We'll talk about that later, $son. We have to do what Damon says and leave the planet. I'll start packing some things. $name_sis, can you please help me?<</speech>>

Your sister nods and the two of them hurry to start packing. You can't help but worry about your dad and what might happen to him. You hope that wherever he is, he is safe.

After a rushed and hectic ten minutes of packing and preparing, you and your family are ready to leave. You say goodbye to your home not knowing when you will be able to return.

<<speech "damon" "Damon">>Come on, follow me.<</speech>>

<<button [[Follow Damon|intro3]]>><</button>>

<</narrator>>

passages.name: damon
passages.source_raw: Damon is an old friend of your dad. You have never had much of a relationship with him because he is very reserved but you know he's always there for your family and you can fully trust him.

passages.name: intro3
passages.source_raw:
<><> As you four leave your house you see lots of police around. They are about to enter your house, few minutes later and you would have been thrown into prison, but now they are looking at a empty apartment.
You follow Damon into the hangar, your $mom and $sis close behind you. Damon leads you to a sleek, silver spaceship and hands you the keys. <>Here you go, $name. This is your ride. It's fully stocked with supplies and has everything you need for the journey. I've also programmed a radio signal into it so you can contact me anytime. Just hit this button here and I'll answer on the other end. I know you have a lot of questions, but it's not safe to talk here. I'll answer everything when you and your family are safe. Until then, just keep this radio with you at all times and stay in touch. Okay?<>
You nod, still in shock at the turn of events. You thank Damon and tell him that you will stay in touch. You turn to your $mom and $sis and nod, signaling that it's time to go. The three of you climb aboard the spaceship and strap yourselves in as Damon gives you some last-minute instructions. <>Remember, stay low and avoid any major spaceports or colonies. Keep your radio on at all times and stay in touch. I'll do everything I can to help you from my end. Good luck.<> With that, Damon shuts the door to the spaceship and gives you a salute. You start the engines and lift off, leaving the hangar and your home planet of //<><><>// behind as you set off into the unknown. You can't help but wonder what lies ahead, but you know that you have to stay strong and stay together if you want to make it through this ordeal. < 5>>

passages.name: haven
passages.source_raw:
Haven is your hometown planet, and it's one of the biggest and most important planets in the Human Federation. Located at the heart of the galaxy, Haven is a hub of commerce, science, and culture, and it's home to some of the most advanced research centers and investigative agencies in the known universe.
Despite its size and complexity, Haven is actually a very welcoming and friendly place. The people there are diverse and open-minded, and there is a strong sense of community and pride in the city.

After some time scavenging on various websites you discover some things:
@@color:white; According to legends passed down through generations, Elysium was ruled by a powerful and ambitious king named Khalindor. He was known for his insatiable desire for conquest and had vowed to invade all the worlds in the universe. In the early days of his reign, Khalindor declared war on their neighboring planet, sparking a brutal conflict that lasted for years. However, before he could achieve his goal of conquering the neighboring planet, a devastating cataclysm struck Elysium, transforming the once-beautiful planet into a purple jungle that was highly venomous to the local population. In the wake of this disaster, the surviving inhabitants of Elysium were forced to flee to the safety of an underground city. There they lived, trying to eke out a living in the harsh and unforgiving environment of the purple jungle that covered the planet's surface. Despite the hardship and danger they faced, the people of Elysium never forgot their former glory and the rule of Khalindor. Location: Citadel Penitentiary Facility, Sector 12-D The Citadel Penitentiary Facility, nestled deep within the forsaken Sector 12-D, stands as a fortress of darkness and despair. Constructed in the abandoned remains of an ancient military outpost, its remote location and treacherous terrain make it an ideal choice for isolating high-profile prisoners. This maximum-security facility is renowned for its impenetrable walls and advanced surveillance systems. Guards and Security: Elite Guard Corps: The prison is heavily guarded by an elite corps of trained personnel. These guards are handpicked for their combat skills, ruthless nature, and loyalty to the prison administration. Expect formidable resistance from them during any escape attempt. Energy Shield Perimeter: The Citadel Penitentiary is encircled by a formidable energy shield, rendering physical intrusion nearly impossible. The shield is powered by a complex energy grid, making it resistant to conventional methods of disabling. Escape Attempts: Tunnels: Previous escape attempts have involved elaborate tunnel systems dug from within the prison's subterranean depths. However, these tunnels were discovered and subsequently sealed off, making a similar approach exceedingly challenging. Aerial Extraction: The Citadel Penitentiary's remote location makes it tempting for aerial extraction. However, the facility boasts a sophisticated anti-aircraft defense system, making helicopter rescues nearly impossible without careful planning and strategic diversion. Insider Cooperation: Successful escapes have often relied on insider cooperation. Identifying a sympathetic guard or staff member willing to aid in your father's liberation could be a crucial element of your rescue plan. But if you’ve got the credits, I’ve got the skills.<> <>We’ll make it worth your while, Elara. Just get us what we need.<> Elara grins and starts typing rapidly on her console, lines of code flashing across the screen.
<>Alright, I’m in... Sort of. It looks like Voss is using an encrypted relay in the Yelena System. I can spoof a signal and get us in, but it’ll take a minute. Cover me.<> Suddenly, the alarms blare—looks like Voss’s crew has detected the intrusion and sent a team to the base to shut it down! <>We’ve got company! I’ll cover the door. You handle the rest!<> You and Jaeriss fend off a small squad of pirates who have breached the base while Elara continues hacking.
<>Got it! Voss’s base is hidden in the asteroid belt near the Yelena System. I’ve also got a partial schematic—it looks like there’s a weak spot on the east side, a maintenance hatch that’s less guarded.<> <>Great work, Elara. We’ll take it from here.<> <>Pleasure doing business with you. Try not to die out there.<> With the new intel in hand, you and Jaeriss prepare for the next step: infiltrating the pirate base. <><>

passages.name: chapter2_bar
passages.source_raw:
<> You and Jaeriss decide to head to the seedy cantina on the edge of the rebel base, a place where smugglers, mercenaries, and other unsavory types gather. The air is thick with smoke and the hum of low conversations.
You notice a group of shady characters huddled in a corner, speaking in hushed tones. One of them has a tattoo of a pirate insignia on his arm, he is surely from Voss’s crew.
<>Looks like we found what we’re looking for. Follow my lead.<> Jaeriss nods and follows as you approach the group. <>Evening, fellas. I hear you’ve got connections to Zarek Voss. Maybe you could share some information... for the right price.<> The pirates glance at each other, weighing the situation. One of them, a grizzled veteran with a scar across his face, speaks up. <>Depends on who’s asking... and how much you’re willing to pay.<> Jaeriss toss a credit chip onto the table. <>That enough to loosen those lips?<> The scarred pirate smirks and pockets the chip. <>Alright, friend. Voss’s base is in the asteroid belt near the Yelena System. It’s hidden real good, but there’s a weak spot—a maintenance hatch on the east side. Not many guards, but it’s a tight squeeze. That’s all I know.<> <>That’s all we needed to hear. Thanks for the tip.<> You and Jaeriss turn to leave, but as you do, one of the pirates grabs your arm. <>Hey, if you’re going after Voss, you might want to watch your back. He’s got a reputation for making examples out of people who cross him.<> <>Thanks for the warning. We’ll keep that in mind.<> With the information secured, you and Jaeriss prepare for the next step: infiltrating Voss’s base. <> <>

passages.name: chapter3_stealth
passages.source_raw:
<>You decide to take the stealthy approach, using a cloaked shuttle to approach the base undetected and sneak in through the maintenance hatch. <>Let’s go with stealth. We’ll use a cloaked shuttle and slip in through that maintenance hatch. Less risk of getting caught in a firefight that way.<> Jaeriss nods, agreeing with your choice. <>I like it. We’ll need to move quietly once we’re inside. If we get caught, we’re done for.<> You head to the hangar and prepare a small, cloaked shuttle for departure.
The journey through the asteroid belt is tense, requiring precise navigation to avoid detection by the base’s scanners. After a nerve-wracking flight, you finally reach the base’s eastern side, where the maintenance hatch is located. You dock the shuttle silently, and you and Jaeriss exit, moving carefully towards the hatch. The metal hatch looms before you, partially obscured by shadows.
<>Here it is. Stay close, and let’s move quickly but quietly. We need to find that artifact before anyone notices we’re here.<> You and Jaeriss slip into the hatch, entering a dimly lit maintenance corridor. The sounds of the base’s operations hum around you—machinery whirring, distant footsteps echoing through the metallic halls. You carefully navigate the narrow corridors, avoiding patrolling guards and bypassing security doors with precise hacking. At one point, you come across a locked door with a complex security code. Jaeriss quickly moves to the control panel. <>I’ve got this. Just keep an eye out.<> After a few tense moments, the door unlocks with a soft beep, and you slip inside undetected. The path ahead is clear, but you hear voices echoing from a nearby corridor.
<>Sounds like some guards up ahead. Let’s wait for them to pass.<> You and Jaeriss hold your breath as two pirate guards walk past, oblivious to your presence. Once they’re gone, you continue your stealthy advance toward the central chamber. With careful movements and a bit of luck, you manage to avoid detection entirely, reaching the door to the central chamber where the Orb of Andarix is kept. The chamber is heavily guarded, and you know the hardest part is yet to come. <>There it is, the central chamber. The Orb should be inside. passages.name: chapter3_assault
passages.source_raw:
<>You decide that a direct assault is the best approach. The ship roars to life, and you set a course for Voss’s base, charging weapons and shields.
As you approach, you open fire on the base's outer defenses, targeting their turrets and shield generators. The base’s alarms blare, and you hear the sounds of scrambling pirates over the comms.
<>Target their shields! Jaeriss, be ready to move the moment we breach.<> <>On it! Let’s hope they’re not expecting this kind of assault.<> After a fierce exchange of fire, you manage to punch a hole through the base’s defenses, creating an opening. You land your ship inside the breached hangar, and the two of you disembark, weapons drawn.
Inside the base, chaos erupts. Pirates scramble to respond to the sudden attack. You and Jaeriss fight your way through waves of pirates, pushing deeper into the base towards the artifact’s location. You move quickly through the lower levels of the base, blasting through small groups of pirates. The air is thick with smoke and the smell of scorched metal. <>Keep moving! We need to reach the central chamber before they regroup.<> <>Right behind you!<> You and Jaeriss push forward, using your combined skills to take down any resistance that comes your way. Eventually, you reach a large blast door. Behind it lies the central chamber where the Orb of Andarix is kept. <>This is it. The Orb is just beyond this door. Ready, $name?<> With weapons drawn and adrenaline pumping, you prepare for the final confrontation with Zarek Voss. <> <>

passages.name: chapter5_confrontation
passages.source_raw:
<> You and Jaeriss stand before the large blast door that guards the central chamber. The air is thick with tension, and you can hear the faint hum of machinery and voices from within. <>This is it, $name. The Orb of Andarix is inside. Be ready. Zarek Voss won’t give it up without a fight.<> <>I’m ready. Let’s do this.<> With a nod, you activate the door controls. The blast door slowly grinds open, revealing a large, dimly lit chamber. At the center of the room, on a pedestal surrounded by glowing blue light, sits the Orb of Andarix.
Standing in front of the Orb, flanked by two heavily armed pirate guards, is Zarek Voss himself. He’s a menacing figure, his body partially enhanced with cybernetics—a glowing red eye, a mechanical arm bristling with weapons, and a personal shield generator humming around him. <>So, you’re the ones causing all this trouble. His guards move forward, weapons raised, and the room explodes into chaos. <><>

passages.name: fight_zarek
passages.source_raw:
<>You and Jaeriss spring into action. You take cover behind a nearby column as the pirate guards open fire, blaster bolts ricocheting off the walls. Jaeriss moves to flank them, her movements swift and precise. <>Jaeriss, take out the guards! I’ll handle Voss!<> You dart out from cover, firing your blaster at Zarek. You roll to the side, dodging the attack, and fire a few more shots at Voss’s shield. Meanwhile, Jaeriss engages the guards in close combat, taking them down one by one with precise strikes and blaster fire. <>Guards are down! It’s just you and him now, $name!<> You nod, focusing on Voss. His shield is starting to flicker, weakening with every hit. You need to disable it before you can land a clean shot. <>Keep the pressure on him! I’ll take out his shield generator!<> You sprint towards Voss, dodging another barrage of projectiles. As you get close, you spot the shield generator mounted on his back, a small device emitting a soft, blue glow. You take aim and fire a concentrated burst at the generator. With a crackle and a burst of sparks, the generator overloads, and Voss’s shield collapses. <>You’ll pay for that!<> Voss charges at you, his cybernetic arm raised. This means more to me and my people than you could ever know.<> <>I’m just glad we made it out alive. passages.name: mq_16_blueprint

passages.source_raw:
<>Your ship enters the swirling gases of the Zarnak Nebula. Visibility is low, and your sensors struggle to cut through the interference. Suddenly, your comms crackle to life, and a stern voice fills the cockpit. <>This is Captain Vexx of the Scavenger’s Wrath. You’re entering my territory, stranger. State your business or prepare to be boarded.<> <>Captain Vexx, I’ve heard of you. I’m here to make a deal. There’s a Federation convoy passing through soon. I want to cause a distraction, and I’m willing to split the spoils with you.<> <>Heh, you’ve got guts coming here with a proposal like that. Alright, I’m listening. What kind of distraction are we talking about?<> <>I need your help to create a diversion big enough to draw their attention away from a high-security target. I hear you’ve got someone on your crew who’s good with explosives.<> Vexx pauses for a moment, then laughs. <>Ah, you must mean Tek-Tek. He’s a bit of an oddball, but he’s the best damn explosives expert this side of the galaxy. Alright, I’ll play along. Meet me on my flagship, and we’ll talk more.<> You dock with Vexx’s flagship and are escorted to a cluttered workshop filled with various gadgets and half-finished projects. At the center of the chaos is Tek-Tek, a short, wiry figure with a wild grin.
<>Oh-ho! What have we here? A new face, and a pretty one at that! So, you want some of Tek-Tek’s famous distraction devices, huh? What’s in it for me?<> <>A share of the convoy loot and maybe a chance to blow some stuff up. Sound good?<> <>Blowing stuff up? That’s my favorite! Alright, I’m in! But first, I need some parts. There’s a scrap field near here with just what I need. Help me get them, and I’ll make you the best damn distractions you’ve ever seen!<> You agree to help Tek-Tek, and the two of you set out to the nearby scrap field. It’s filled with derelict ships and discarded technology, perfect for scavenging.
<>Alright, Tek-Tek, what are we looking for?<> <>See those ion capacitors over there? And the plasma coils? Those babies will make the perfect base for our distractions. Grab as many as you can find, and watch out for the scavenger drones. They don’t like sharing.<> You navigate through the debris, avoiding the aggressive scavenger drones and collecting the necessary parts. After a few close calls and some creative thinking, you manage to gather everything Tek-Tek needs. <>Got the parts. Now, let’s see what you can do.<> Back at the workshop, Tek-Tek gets to work, his hands moving with surprising speed and precision. Soon, he’s crafted several distraction devices—flash bombs, noise makers, and a few other surprises. <>Here you go! These babies will light up the sky and give those Federation dogs something to think about. Just make sure you’re not too close when they go off. They pack a punch!<> <>Thanks, Tek-Tek. These should do nicely.<> Captain Vexx comes to the workshop to say goodbye. <>Glad you found what you needed, young man. We are having a party today on the ship, I want you to stay as a guest of mine. You won't regret it.<> Should you get back with Gemma or stay and party with Captain Vexx? <> <> <>

passages.name: mq17_gemma
passages.source_raw:
<><>With the digging equipment securely in hand, you return to the rebel base, where Gemma is eagerly waiting in her workshop. The equipment was a bit rusty, but it was still in good working condition, and that’s what mattered.
Gemma looks up from her work as you enter, a smile spreading across her face. <>You’re back! And I see you’ve got the goods. How’d it go out there?<> <>It wasn’t easy, but I got the equipment. We’ll need to make some modifications, but it should work for what we need.<> <>Great job, $name! I knew you could do it. Let’s take a look...<> You hand over the digging equipment, and Gemma begins examining it, checking for structural integrity and potential modifications. <>Hmm, a bit old, but definitely sturdy. We’ll need to upgrade the power cells and reinforce the drill bits to handle the tougher sections of rock. But this should do nicely.<> <>What’s next on the list?<> <>Next, we’ll need Concealment Materials. The tunnel isn’t just going to be a straight shot—we’ll need to hide our work and make sure we aren’t detected. There’s a contact of ours on Duststar, a small moon known for its black market in stealth tech and camouflage materials.<> <>Duststar, huh? Sounds like a fun place.<> <>Oh, it’s a barrel of laughs, alright. Watch your back, though. The people there aren’t exactly friendly to strangers, and you’ll have to deal with Vix, a master of deception and stealth. She’s our best shot at getting what we need.<> <>Got it. I’ll head there now and see what I can find.<> <>Be careful, $name. And good luck. We’re getting close, I can feel it.<> With your next objective clear, you head back to your ship and set course for Duststar, ready for whatever challenges lie ahead. <><> <><>After securing the distraction mechanisms with the help of Captain Vexx and Tek-Tek, you return to the rebel base. As you enter the hangar, you see Gemma waiting for you with an eager expression.
<>You’re back! And you’ve got the goods. I was starting to worry—how did it go out there?<> <>It was a bit touch and go, but I got the distraction devices. They should be enough to draw attention away from the prison during our approach.<> <>Fantastic! These look perfect. Tek-Tek did a good job with these. We’ll set them up to go off in key locations and create the chaos we need.<> <>What’s the next step?<> <>Next, we need a Helicopter Expert, someone who knows how to pilot and maneuver through the dense anti-aircraft defenses around the Citadel. There’s a pilot I know on Stellar Drift, a rogue asteroid station known for housing ex-military types. Captain Eris Dray, is the best there is when it comes to evasive maneuvers. She used to be Federation but went rogue after a falling out with her superiors.<> <>Sounds like my kind of person. How do I convince her to help?<> <>Eris is a bit of a wild card. She doesn’t trust easily, but she has a soft spot for underdogs and people who aren’t afraid to stand up to authority. You’ll have to win her over. And be ready, she likes to test people to see if they’re worth her time.<> <>Alright, I’ll head to Stellar Drift and see if I can convince her to join us.<> <>Good luck, $name. If anyone can persuade her, it’s you. Just… don’t let her get the upper hand. She’s known for her mind games.<> With a nod, you head back to your ship, setting a course for Stellar Drift. Convincing Captain Eris Dray to join your mission might be your toughest challenge yet. <><> <><> <>

passages.name: mq17_mining_colony2
passages.source_raw:
<>Intrigued by her sudden change in demeanor, you agree and follow Silva to her bedroom located deep within the mining complex. Once inside, she closes the door behind you, leaving you alone together in the small room lit only by a flickering candle. She moves closer to you, fixing you with an intense gaze as she takes off her gloves, exposing calloused hands, signs of a life spent working hard in harsh conditions. <>I can't see a coffee machine here...<> Leaning against the wall, she crosses her arms over her chest and asks: <>Do you really think we are going to drink some coffee?<> Her voice has dropped an octave, becoming husky and seductive. Before you can respond, she steps forward, closing the distance between you two. Her hand reaches out to touch your face gently, tracing down your jawline. Then, without warning, she drops to her knees. With nimble fingers, she begins undoing your belt buckle and pulling down your pants, followed quickly by your underwear.
As Silva pulls down your pants and underwear, her eyes never leave yours. Without breaking eye contact, she leans forward and wraps her lips around your shaft.
The sensation sends shivers down your spine. Slowly, sensually, she starts to move her head back and forth, taking you deeper into her mouth each time until you hit the back of her throat.
Suddenly, you can hold back no longer. With a loud groan, you release everything you've been holding onto.
Silva doesn't falter; instead, she swallows eagerly, drinking every drop you offer. When you finally finish, she slowly releases you from her mouth, licking her lips clean.
Breathlessly, you pull up your pants and try to gather your thoughts. Women alone deep in this mining colony surely can be horny... I better get back to the base. <> <>

<> Vexx leads you through the ship’s narrow corridors to a spacious cargo bay that has been transformed into a lively party space. The room is filled with pirates and scavengers from all walks of life, laughing, drinking, and dancing to the beat of a raucous band playing on a makeshift stage.
The atmosphere is electric, a mix of camaraderie and wild abandon. Vexx gestures for you to join in. <>Enjoy yourself, $name. Tonight, we celebrate another successful raid! Feel free to mingle with my crew. You never know what kind of useful information you might pick up.<>
After a bit of drinking and partying, Vexx calls your name. <>$name ! Come here, dude!<>
<>This girl here told me she won't do anything with me tonight... UNLESS YOU JOIN US!<> <> <> <>

passages.name: mq18_duststar
passages.source_raw:
<>The narrow alley is dimly lit, the faint glow of neon signs casting eerie shadows on the walls. As you approach the hooded figure, they turn to face you, their eyes hidden beneath the shadow of the hood.
<>You must be the one Gemma sent. Bold move, coming here alone. What do you want?<> <>I need concealment materials—top of the line. I heard you’re the person to talk to.<> Vix chuckles softly, a sound that sends a chill down your spine. <>You heard right. But nothing comes free, especially not here. You want my help, you’ll need to prove you’re worth my time.<> <>What do you have in mind?<> Vix steps closer, her voice dropping to a whisper. <>There’s a job I’ve been planning. A little retrieval mission. There’s an old facility on the other side of the moon, heavily guarded. Inside, there’s a piece of tech I need. You help me get it, and I’ll give you the materials you’re looking for.<> <>Sounds like a deal. What’s the catch?<> <>The facility is protected by a cloaking field and patrolled by mercenaries. It’s not just about getting in. It’s about getting in undetected. I want to see if you’re as good as Gemma says.<> You nod, understanding the challenge ahead. <>Alright, I’m in. Lead the way.<> Vix nods and motions for you to follow. You make your way through the market streets to a secluded area where a small, sleek ship is hidden. You both board and head towards the old facility, the moon’s barren landscape stretching out before you.
As you approach the facility, Vix activates a stealth cloak around the ship, making it nearly invisible to sensors. <>Alright, here’s the plan. We get in, grab the tech, and get out before they even know we’re there. Stay close and keep quiet.<> You and Vix move through the facility’s perimeter, avoiding patrols and using the shadows to your advantage. You spot a security console ahead, and Vix motions for you to disable it. <>I’ll take care of it. Cover me.<> <> <>

passages.name: mq18_stellar_drift
passages.source_raw:
<>The central hub is filled with the hum of conversations and the occasional clink of glasses.
You spot Captain Eris Dray at a corner table, nursing a drink and watching the crowd with a sharp, calculating gaze.
<>Captain Dray, I presume?<> <>Who’s asking?<> <>Name’s $name. I hear you’re the best helicopter pilot around, and I could use your help.<> Eris smirks, her eyes narrowing as she assesses you. <>You’ve got guts coming here, asking for my help. But I don’t just work with anyone. I need to know you can handle yourself. I’ve got a little test in mind—think you’re up for it?<> <>What kind of test?<> <>A dogfight simulation. You and me, one-on-one. Show me you’ve got the skills to fly with me, and maybe we’ll talk about your little mission.<> You nod, understanding the challenge. <>Alright, I’m game. Let’s do it.<> Eris leads you to a small simulator room at the back of the hub. The room is filled with advanced equipment, and Eris quickly sets up the simulation.
<>Get ready, $name. This won’t be easy.<> The simulation begins, and you find yourself in a virtual cockpit, navigating through a dense asteroid field while trying to evade Eris’s attacks. <> <>

passages.name: mq18_gemma
passages.source_raw:
<><>After successfully acquiring the concealment materials from Vix, you return to the rebel base, feeling a sense of accomplishment. You make your way to Gemma’s workshop, where she’s already busy working on the modifications for the digging equipment.
Gemma looks up as you enter, a glint of excitement in her eyes. <>You’re back! And I see you’ve got the materials. How did it go on Duststar?<> <>It was a bit tricky, but I managed to get what we need. Vix sends her regards.<> <>Typical Vix. Always likes to test people. But if you passed her test, then you must have done something right. Let me see what you got.<> You hand over the concealment materials, and Gemma inspects them closely, nodding with approval. <>This is perfect. With these, we can make sure the tunnel stays hidden and undetected while we dig. We’re almost ready, $name. All we need now is to finalize our plan with Jasper and get this operation underway.<> <>Agreed. I’ll go talk to Jasper and get things started.<> <>Good idea. He’s been working on some last-minute intel that might be useful for the mission. Head over to his quarters—he’s expecting you.<> With the final preparations nearly complete, you head out of Gemma’s workshop and make your way towards Jasper’s quarters. It’s time to get this mission underway and start the rescue operation. <><><>With Captain Eris Dray agreeing to join the mission, you return to the rebel base, feeling a sense of confidence in your plan. You head straight to Gemma’s workshop, where she’s eagerly awaiting your return.
Gemma looks up as you enter, a smile spreading across her face. <>You’re back! And I see you’ve brought a new friend.<> <>This is Captain Eris Dray. She’s agreed to help us with the extraction. I think we’ve got ourselves a solid team now.<> <>I don’t work with amateurs, Gemma. You know that. But I have to say, $name here showed some real skills. I’m in, but we better have a damn good plan.<> <>Don’t worry, Eris. We’ve got a good plan. But we still need to go over the final details with Jasper. He’s been gathering some last-minute intel that could help us get through this in one piece.<> <>I’ll head over to Jasper’s quarters and see what he’s got. Time to get this operation rolling.<> <>Good idea. We’re almost there, $name. Let’s make sure everything’s set before we move out.<> With your team assembled and ready, you make your way out of Gemma’s workshop and head towards Jasper’s quarters. It’s time to finalize the plan and begin the mission. <><><> <>

passages.name: mq19_jasper_quarters
passages.source_raw:
<><><>I have everything ready to execute out plan.<> <>Hmmm... I think there is still one thing for you to do. Do you know Jaeriss? That blue strange woman on the base, she can be useful for us, but she needs some help. Can you take care of that first?<> <>Sure thing, Jasper. I'll get back to you.<> <>Thanks, my boy.<> <><>You enter Jasper’s quarters, the room filled with various maps, charts, and documents. Jasper is standing over a large map of the Citadel Penitentiary, studying it intently. He looks up as you enter, a serious expression on his face.
<>Ah, $name. Just the person I wanted to see. I hear you’ve been making good progress with Gemma on the tunnel escape plan.<> <>That’s right. We’ve got the blueprint, the digging equipment, and the concealment materials. We’re ready to start digging, but we need to make sure we’re not missing anything before we move forward.<> Jasper nods, a thoughtful look on his face as he examines the map. <>You’ve done well so far, $name. But this next step is critical. The Citadel’s underground sensors are highly sensitive. If we’re not careful, they’ll detect any vibrations or movement from the tunnel.<> <>We’ve got the concealment materials to mask our progress, but we’ll need to dig carefully to avoid triggering any alarms.<> <>Exactly. I’ve been looking over the latest intel, and there’s a security shift change happening in about 48 hours. That’s our best window. During the shift change, there’s a brief period where the security systems reset. It’s a narrow window, but if we time it right, we can make significant progress without being detected.<> <>So we start digging during the shift change. Got it. What about the guards? They’re bound to patrol the perimeter.<> <>We’ve got a small team ready to create a distraction if necessary. A false flag operation to draw the guards away from the tunnel entry point. It’ll buy you some time, but you’ll need to be quick.<> <>Alright, sounds like we have a solid plan. I’ll get the team ready and start the final preparations.<> Jasper nods, his expression serious. <>Remember, $name, this mission is personal for all of us. Your father believed in this cause, and we believe in you. Stay focused, and don’t take unnecessary risks. We’re counting on you to get this right.<> <>I won’t let you down, Jasper. We’re going to bring him back.<> Jasper smiles, a hint of pride in his eyes. <>I know you won’t. Now, go get ready. We move out at first light.<> With a nod, you turn and head back to prepare for the tunnel dig. The fate of your father, and perhaps the entire rebel cause, rests on your shoulders. <> <><>You step into Jasper’s quarters, finding him reviewing several data pads spread out across his desk. He glances up as you enter, a look of determination in his eyes.
<>There you are, $name. I hear you’ve got Captain Dray on board for the extraction. That’s good news.<> <>Yeah, she’s agreed to help. We’ve got the distraction mechanisms ready, and she’s confident she can navigate through the anti-aircraft defenses. We just need to finalize the plan.<> Jasper nods, motioning you over to his desk. <>Take a look at this. We’ve got new intel on the Citadel Penitentiary’s airspace defenses. They’ve recently upgraded their AA systems with a new type of targeting software—makes them faster, more accurate. But there’s a weakness in their coverage pattern here.<> He points to a specific section on the map—a blind spot near the northwestern perimeter of the prison. <>It’s a small gap, but it’s there. If Captain Dray can get the helicopter through this zone without triggering their sensors, she should be able to reach the extraction point undetected. The distraction devices you acquired will be crucial in drawing their fire away.<> <>And what about ground support? We’re going to need someone to handle things from the inside.<> <>We’ve got an insider contact already in place, but we’ll need to sync up with them once you’re close. The encrypted communicator you got will ensure we maintain a secure line. Timing is everything, $name. You and Captain Dray need to be perfectly in sync with the ground team.<> <>Understood. What’s our timeline?<> <>We move at dawn, 36 hours from now. That’s when their AA systems run their routine maintenance check. During that time, their sensors will be at minimal capacity. It’s a short window, but it’s our best shot.<> <>Got it. I’ll get Captain Dray and the team ready. We won’t miss our chance.<> Jasper nods, a determined look on his face. <>Good. This mission is too important to fail. Your father’s life depends on it, and so does our fight against the Federation. Stay sharp, and remember—we’re counting on you.<> <>I won’t let you down, Jasper. We’re bringing him back.<> Jasper places a reassuring hand on your shoulder. <>I know you will, $name. Now, go get ready. We have a lot of work ahead of us.<> You nod, turning to leave Jasper’s quarters. The weight of the mission is heavy on your shoulders, but you feel ready. It’s time to prepare for the aerial extraction. <> <><><>

passages.name: rebelbase_walk
passages.source_raw:
<><><> There is nothing much more to see here. You've met many of the people who call this place home and helped out where you could. <> <><>As you wander through the base, you notice a group of young friends playing. One of the boys, a fellow named Tarek, seems to be struggling with a small drone, trying to make it fly. <>Come on, you piece of junk... work!<> You approach and offer to help. <>Need a hand with that?<> <>Yeah, it’s my dad’s old drone. He used to fix it for me, but I don’t know how. Can you help me?<> You decide to assist Tarek, tinkering with the drone’s controls and adjusting its circuits. After a few moments, the drone springs to life, hovering in the air.
<>Wow! Thank you so much! You’re the best!<> You smile, feeling a sense of warmth from his joy.
@@color:deepskyblue;Intelligence increased!@@
<><><> <> <><>While walking through the base, you come across Tania, one of the rebel medics, frantically looking around. <>Oh no, where is it? I can’t find it!<> <>Is something wrong?<> <>I’ve lost my datapad, and it has all my medical notes on it. If I don’t find it soon, I won’t be able to prepare the treatments we need!<> You decide to help Tania search for her datapad. After a few minutes of looking around the common areas and medbay, you find it wedged under a chair.
<>Is this what you’re looking for?<> <>Yes! Oh, thank you so much, $name! You’ve saved me a lot of trouble.<> Tania smiles gratefully, and you feel a small sense of satisfaction from helping out. <> <> <><>As you stroll through a quieter part of the base, you hear the faint sound of music coming from a nearby room. Curious, you follow the sound and find Renn, a young rebel engineer, playing an old acoustic guitar.
<>Oh, hey there. Didn’t think anyone would find me back here. I like to play when things get too hectic around here.<> <>You’re pretty good. Mind if I listen for a bit?<> Renn smiles and continues to play a soft, soothing melody. The music is a welcome reprieve from the tension of the upcoming mission, and you feel a sense of calm washing over you. <>Thanks for listening, $name. Sometimes it feels good to just… relax for a moment, you know?<> You nod, appreciating the brief moment of peace. <> <> <><> Walking near the base's storage area, you see a small commotion. A group of rebels is gathered around Kara, a tough-looking woman who seems to be organizing a boxing match. <>Alright, who’s next? Come on, don’t be shy! Step up and show us what you’re made of!<> The rebels cheer and encourage one another. Feeling the need for a bit of exercise and perhaps to blow off some steam, you decide to join in. After they all leave and it's just Kara and you, you step into the ring. <>I’ll give it a shot.<> Kara grins and hands you some boxing gloves. <>Alright, but let me get comfortable,<> She takes her top off, leaving you with your mouth wide open, she just giggles and begins trying to land a strike on you.
After a few minutes, you both are getting tired. For a second, you lose concentration by staring at her boobs, just the time needed for her to land a winning blow on your face. <>Nice one, $name! You’ve got some moves! But, unluckily for you, I win!<> <>I would have done better if i could concentrate.<> <>Excuses, excuses...<>
@@color:#e8c320;Strengh increased!@@
<><><><> <> <><>While exploring the base, you find yourself in the engineering bay, where you see Juliana, a veteran mechanic, working on a new prototype vehicle. <>Hey, $name! Good to see you. I’m working on a new scout vehicle that could really use a test run. You up for it?<>
<>Absolutely. I’d love to see what this baby can do.<> You hop into the vehicle, and Juliana directs you to the makeshift course set up just outside the base. The scout vehicle handles smoothly, and you maneuver it through the course, testing its agility and speed. After a thrilling run, you stop the engine. <>Not bad! With a few more tweaks, this thing could be a game-changer for our recon missions.<> You nod, feeling good about contributing to the base’s efforts in a small but meaningful way. <>Let me thank you properly for your help today...<> <> <><><>While wandering near the base’s communication center, you notice Layla, a young communications officer, furiously typing away at her console. She looks frustrated.
<>Ugh, this encryption code is driving me crazy! If I can’t break it soon, we’ll lose the chance to intercept an important enemy transmission.<> <>Need a fresh pair of eyes on that?<> <>Yes, please! I could use all the help I can get right now.<> You sit down beside her and start analyzing the encryption patterns.
After a few minutes of intense focus, you manage to crack the code. <>You did it, $name! We’re in! This is going to be a game-changer for our next operation.<> Layla beams at you, clearly impressed by your skills. You feel a rush of satisfaction from the accomplishment.

passages.name: rebelbase_sisbar
passages.source_raw:
<>You decide to take a break from the daily grind of life and invite your $sis, $name_sis, to join you for a night out. She smiles when you suggest heading to the bar, clearly ready for a fun evening. <>I could definitely use a break. Let’s go have some fun, $name!<> The two of you make your way through the winding corridors of the base, eventually arriving at the lively bar area. The room is filled with rebels unwinding after a long day—some are playing darts, others are chatting loudly over drinks, and a few are even dancing to the upbeat music playing in the background. <>What are you drinking tonight, $name_sis?<> <>I think I’ll start with something strong. How about a Corellian whiskey?<> You nod and order two drinks from the bartender. As you hand her the whiskey, you raise your glass in a toast.

passages.name: mq21_talk_mom
passages.source_raw:
<>The tense atmosphere aboard your ship slowly begins to dissipate as the dust settles from the rescue mission. You and the team have returned safely to the rebel base, but the triumphant feeling of success is overshadowed by the one devastating realization: your father wasn’t there.
The mission had been perfectly executed—every distraction, every move planned to the second. You had breached the Citadel Penitentiary, navigated its labyrinthine corridors, and faced down its elite guards. But the cell where your father was supposed to be held was empty, and his name had been wiped from the records. You sit in the ship’s cockpit, staring blankly out at the stars, lost in thought. Your mother joins you, her face etched with concern and weariness. <>I’m so sorry, $name. I know how much you wanted to find him… how much we both did.<> <>It doesn’t make any sense, $mom. All the intel pointed to him being there. We did everything right, and still… he wasn’t there.<> She places a comforting hand on your shoulder, her eyes filled with a mix of empathy and determination.
<>I know, $name. But we can’t give up. This just means we need to look elsewhere. There must be another clue, another lead… something we’ve overlooked.<> You nod, though the frustration and disappointment still churn inside you. <>But where? We’ve followed every lead, checked every possible location… What if… what if he’s…<> Your voice trails off, the weight of the thought too heavy to finish. Your mother gives your shoulder a reassuring squeeze. <>Don’t think like that, $name. Your father is out there. I can feel it. And I think… I think I might know where we should look next.<> <>Where?<> She takes a deep breath, her gaze drifting out towards the endless void of space. <>Veldara V. It’s a desert planet, far off in the outer systems. It was once a thriving colony, a place your father and I called home when you were young. We were working on a top-secret project there, one that… well, it didn’t end the way we hoped.<> <>I’ve heard you talk about Veldara V before, but only in passing. Why do you think he might be there?<> She sighs, a hint of regret in her expression. <>There were things we left behind when we were forced to evacuate. Personal things… but also information, data that could be crucial. If your father ever needed to hide, or leave a message for us, that’s where he would do it. There’s something there, a music box with a recording of his voice. He left it for me, in case something happened.<> <>A music box? Why haven’t we gone there before?<> <>Because I was afraid, $name. Afraid of what I might find… or what I might not find. But now, I think it’s our best chance. We need to go there. We need to find that box and see what your father left for us.<> You nod, understanding the gravity of her words. The idea of going to a place so tied to your family’s past is daunting, but if there’s any chance of finding a clue about your father’s whereabouts, you’re willing to take it. <>Alright, $mom. Let’s do it. Let’s go to Veldara V and find this music box. If there’s even a chance it could lead us to Dad, it’s worth it.<> <>Thank you, $name. I know this isn’t easy… but we have to keep going. For him. And for us.<> You both rise from your seats, moving to the navigation console. You enter the coordinates for Veldara V, your hands steady, but your mind racing with thoughts of what you might find there.
<>Coordinates set. We should be there in a few hours.<> <>Good. Let’s get some rest on the way. We’ll need all our strength for what’s ahead.<> You nod, feeling a mixture of determination and uncertainty. As the ship lifts off and breaks free of the rebel base, you glance at your $mom. Despite the years and the hardships, she still carries a strength that inspires you—a strength you know you’ll need for the journey ahead. And what to say about her looks... she is amazing. <>We’ll find him, $mom. No matter what it takes.<> <>Yes, we will, $name. Together.<> The ship accelerates, and the stars outside stretch into lines of light as you enter hyperspace, your destination set, and your hearts steeled for whatever awaits you on Veldara V. <> <>

passages.name: mq21_desert_landing
passages.source_raw:
<>The barren desert planet of Veldara V stretches out before you as your ship descends through the thick, swirling dust clouds. The atmosphere outside is harsh, filled with a hot, dry wind that sweeps across the endless dunes, carving deep valleys into the rugged landscape. Your $mom, seated beside you in the cockpit, stares intently out the viewport, her face etched with a mixture of nostalgia and determination.
<>Are you sure this is where you want to be?<> <>Yes, $name. I’m sure. Veldara V was once our home—your father and I spent years here, working on a top-secret project. This place holds so many memories… and something important I left behind.<> <>What did you leave behind?<> <>A music box. It was a gift from your father. It has a recorded message from him, something I haven’t listened to in years. I need to hear his voice again… to remember why we started all this in the first place.<> You nod, understanding her need to reconnect with the past. As you leave the ship, you can see the ruins of what was once a thriving colony. A few crumbling buildings, scattered debris, and the rusted remains of large laboratory structures barely visible beneath the layers of sand. The heat is immediate, intense, and unforgiving. <>Wow, this place is even more desolate than I imagined… Hard to believe people once lived here.<> <>It wasn’t always like this. Veldara V was once a hub of scientific research and innovation. We worked on so many things… some good, some I’d rather forget. But it was home.<> She takes a deep breath, shielding her eyes from the sun as she looks around, taking in the sight of the decaying remnants of the colony.
<>Come on, the labs are this way. If the music box is still here, it’ll be in our old quarters, deep in the research complex.<> You follow her lead, moving across the cracked and dusty ground towards the larger buildings that once housed laboratories and living quarters for the colony’s scientists. The air is thick with dust, making it hard to see far ahead, but you can make out the faint outline of a sprawling complex partially buried under the encroaching dunes. <>You and Dad really spent years here, huh? What were you working on that was so important?<> <>A lot of things, $name. Some of them classified even now. But there was one project—something that could change the course of history. Your father believed in it… but not everyone agreed with him. That’s when things started to fall apart.<> As you approach the entrance to the old research complex, you can see it’s partially caved in. You and your $mom begin to clear away some of the debris, revealing a rusted door hanging off its hinges. The remnants of the colony loom large around you, shadows stretching long in the harsh sunlight. <>Let’s hope the music box is still where you left it. If the scavengers haven’t already taken it…<> <>I have a feeling it’s still here. Some things have a way of staying hidden until they’re meant to be found.<> You push the door open with a creaking groan, stepping inside the darkened hallway of the old research complex. The air is cooler here, the sunlight barely penetrating the thick layers of sand that cover the windows. Broken equipment and abandoned crates line the walls, evidence of a hasty evacuation years ago.
<>Which way to the quarters?<> <>Down this hall, to the right. But stay alert, this place has been abandoned for years, and who knows what could be lurking in the shadows… or who might have set up camp here.<> You move cautiously through the narrow corridor, your footsteps echoing softly in the silence. The air feels heavy with the weight of the past, and you can sense your mother’s unease as she glances around, taking in the familiar but faded surroundings. <>So much has changed… and yet, it’s like time stood still. Your father… he would have wanted to see this place again, too. To remember what we were trying to do here.<> Suddenly, you hear faint voices coming from deeper within the complex. You stop, motioning for your $mom to stay quiet as you listen. The voices are rough, and they’re getting closer. <>Sounds like someone’s here… We should be careful.<> Your $mom nods, and you both press against the wall, peering around the corner. Down the hall, you see a group of scavengers, three of them, picking through the debris and chatting loudly.
<>Check this out. Bet we could get a good price for some of this stuff. Old tech always fetches a nice sum.<> <>Yeah, and what about that ship we saw outside? Think they’ve got anything worth taking?<> <>Who cares? If they’re dumb enough to leave it unguarded, it’s ours for the taking. Let’s see if we can find its owners first. Might be fun…<> Your blood runs cold at the suggestion. You step forward, blocking their path, your hand on your blaster. <>That’s close enough. This is private business. Move along, and no one gets hurt.<> The scavengers stop, surprised at first, but then their surprise turns into sneers. <>Look who we have here. A hero wannabe. And who’s that hiding behind you? Your girlfriend? She got a nice pair of tits.<> <>Or maybe it’s his mama. Doesn’t matter. She looks like she could use some company… And I could do with some dick sucking.<> You feel a surge of anger as the scavengers make lewd comments, their tone mocking and malicious. Your $mom’s expression remains calm, but you can see a flicker of discomfort in her eyes. <>She is mine, and mine only. Back off. Now.<> The scavengers chuckle, clearly not taking you seriously. <>Or what, kid? You gonna shoot us all by yourself?<> You draw your blaster, the barrel steady, your eyes locked on the scavenger who spoke.
<>If I have to. Last warning. Leave.<> The scavengers glance at each other, their expressions hardening. They’re not backing down. You know you have to act quickly to protect your mother. You fire a warning shot that hits the ground near their feet, sending a shower of dust and debris into the air. <>Alright, kid, you wanna play tough? Let’s see what you got!<> They charge at you, weapons drawn, but you’re ready. You fire another shot, hitting the closest scavenger in the leg, causing him to collapse with a scream. The others hesitate, momentarily taken aback by your quick reaction.
<>$name! Behind you!<> You spin around just in time to dodge a knife aimed at your back. You quickly disarm the attacker, delivering a swift kick to his chest that sends him sprawling into a pile of debris. The last scavenger, seeing his comrades incapacitated, raises his hands defensively. <>Alright, alright! We’re leaving! Just… don’t shoot!<> <>Get out. Now.<> The scavengers retreat, dragging their wounded friend with them. You lower your blaster, breathing heavily, adrenaline still coursing through your veins. <>You handled that well. You’ve grown up so much…<> <>I wasn’t going to let them hurt you, $name_mom.<> Your $mom smiles softly, a look of pride in her eyes. <>Thank you, $name. Now, let’s find that music box. It should be just up ahead.<> With the scavengers dealt with, you and your $mom continue deeper into the complex, ready to uncover the secrets of the past and the message left behind by your father. <> <>

passages.name: mq21_vault
passages.source_raw:
<>The next morning, the harsh sunlight filters through the cracks in the walls of the old quarters, waking you from a restless sleep. Your $mom is already up, packing up the few supplies you have. Maybe even find love again, if that’s what you want. I would never want you to be alone, my love. You’ve always been the strongest person I’ve ever known. Keep being strong, for yourself… and for $name.<> The message ends, and the music box falls silent once more. Your $mom sits there, tears streaming down her face, her shoulders shaking with quiet sobs. <>Oh… He is right honey, I'm so sorry for treating you like this all day...<> <>$name_mom… he loved you. She leans into you, holding on tightly, as if afraid to let go. <>I know, $name. passages.name: mq23_raphaella
passages.source_raw:
<>You arrive at Fortunes Told, inside, Raphaella sits behind a table adorned with a deck of tarot cards. She was waiting for you.
<>You are here at last.<> <>Hello, Raphaella. I was wondering if you could see someth-<> She interrupts you mid sentence. <>Your father, yes. I know his wereabouts are what troubles you, $name.<> <>I went looking for him at a high security prison, but I arrived late. They took him to a-<> <>To a black site, yes... Very far...<> <>Yes! That is what I found out. Do you... know more?<> <>Hmmmm...<> She puts her hands on the magic crystal ball in front of her.
<>This black site... It is not what you imagine it to be. I can see sunlight, very bright. He is not alone. He is happy there.<> <>Really?? Is he okay???<> <>Hmmmm... He is not really himself. He is like a shadow of his former person...<> <>What do you mean?? Do you know how to get to him???<> <>Hand me a piece of paper.<> You hand her a piece of paper and she starts writing numbers on it. They look like coordinates.
<>Here you go, kid. I worry that you will find your father there, but your search will not end this soon. Good luck.<> Without really paying attention to Raphaella's warn, you leave Fortunes Told and get back to your ship. <><>

passages.name: elysium_wander
passages.source_raw:
<><><> There doesn’t seem to be much more to do here. You've met many of the unique inhabitants of Elysium and experienced their way of life. <> <><> As you explore the winding streets of Elysium, you stumble upon a small tea house. The scent of freshly brewed tea wafts through the air, drawing you inside. Seated at a corner table is an elderly man in a traditional robe, his eyes closed in meditation.
As you approach, he opens his eyes and gestures for you to join him. <>Welcome, traveler. I am Toshiro, keeper of wisdom and tea. Would you care to share a cup and perhaps gain a bit of enlightenment?<> <>I’d be honored, Toshiro. What wisdom do you have to share?<> Toshiro pours you a cup of tea, his hands steady and precise. You take a sip, feeling a warmth spread through you. <>Life is like a cup of tea, $name. Sometimes bitter, sometimes sweet, but always worth savoring. Remember to find balance in all things, and your journey will be a prosperous one.<> You feel a sense of calm and clarity wash over you as Toshiro speaks. His words resonate deeply, and you realize there is much to learn from this place and its people. <>Thank you, Toshiro. I will remember your words.<> Toshiro smiles and nods, returning to his meditation as you finish your tea.
@@color:deepskyblue;Intelligence increased!@@
<><><> <> <><>Walking through a narrow alley, you notice a young woman performing a delicate fan dance in front of a small crowd. Her movements are graceful and mesmerizing, each step perfectly timed to the soft music playing in the background.
After her performance, she approaches you, her face glowing with a warm smile. <>Thank you for watching my dance, traveller. I am Mei. It is rare to see a new face in Elysium. Would you like to learn a few steps? It’s a wonderful way to express oneself and connect with the spirit of the colony.<> <>I’d love to. I’ve never tried dancing like that before.<> Mei giggles softly and takes your hand, guiding you through a few basic steps. Her touch is light, her instructions clear and encouraging. You find yourself relaxing into the rhythm of the dance. <> <> <><>You wander into a small herbal shop, filled with the scent of various exotic plants and spices. Behind the counter stands an older woman, her hands skillfully mixing ingredients in a mortar and pestle.
<>Welcome, traveler. I am Yumi, the herbalist. I see you have traveled far. Would you like to learn about the healing properties of our herbs? Perhaps you could use a remedy for your journey.<> <>That sounds interesting. I could always use a bit of extra knowledge.<> Yumi nods and begins explaining the different herbs, their uses, and their healing properties. You listen intently, fascinated by her knowledge and expertise. <> <> <><>As you wander through a particularly quiet and dimly lit part of Elysium, a soft, ethereal light begins to glow ahead of you. You pause, intrigued, as the light grows brighter and takes the form of a small, winged figure hovering in the air. She appears almost transparent, with delicate, shimmering wings and a mischievous smile.
<>Hello there, traveler. You don’t look like you belong here. But then again, neither do I, in a way. I’m Amara, a jinx—or as some might call it, a guardian spirit. And you… you are a curious sight indeed!<> <>Amara, huh? I didn’t think spirits were real. What brings you to reveal yourself to me?<> Amara giggles, her voice like a soft chime echoing in the cavernous space. <>Oh, I’m very real, $name. I’ve been watching over this place for more than 200 years now, keeping an eye on these people, guiding them, protecting them. But they can’t see me… They don’t even know I exist. And, quite frankly, it gets dreadfully boring!<> <>So, you’ve been watching over Elysium for centuries, and no one knows you’re here? That sounds… lonely.<> Amara nods, her expression becoming a bit more somber. <>Lonely? Perhaps. Unappreciated? Definitely. But you, you’re different. You’re not from here, and that intrigues me. Tell me, traveler, what is life like outside this hidden world? What wonders have you seen? What dangers have you faced?<> You take a moment to consider her question, thinking back on your journeys through the stars. <>Life outside of Elysium is… vast. There are endless stars, planets with all kinds of environments—deserts, oceans, jungles. Some places are beautiful, and others are dangerous. I’ve faced pirates, hostile aliens, and even corrupt governments. It’s never dull, that’s for sure.<> Amara listens intently, her wings fluttering slightly as if reacting to your words. <>That sounds thrilling. I wish I could see it for myself. But I’m bound to this place, to these people. Even if they can’t see me, they need me. Without me, who knows what could happen?<> <>Why are you bound here, Amara? Is it a choice, or…?<> Amara looks thoughtful for a moment, her gaze distant. <>It’s a bit of both. I was created to protect this place, a guardian woven from magic and will. But over time, I began to care for these people, even if they don’t know I’m here. I chose to stay, to keep watching over them. But sometimes, I wonder what it would be like to be free… to explore like you do.<> You sense a deep yearning in her voice, a desire for freedom she’s never been able to experience. <>If you could leave, where would you go? What would you do?<> <>Oh, I’d fly among the stars, see the worlds you speak of, meet strange beings, learn new things… It would be wonderful! But alas, that is not my fate. At least, not yet.<> <> <> <><>You find yourself near a small dojo, where a group of children are practicing martial arts under the watchful eye of a strict-looking sensei. As you watch, the sensei notices you and approaches.
<>You have the eyes of a warrior, traveler. I am Sensei Hiro. Would you like to spar with me? A friendly match to test your skills.<> <>I’d like that. It’s been a while since I’ve had a good challenge.<> You step onto the mat, facing Sensei Hiro. The children gather around, eager to watch the match. Hiro bows, and you do the same before the sparring begins. <> <><> <><>In a secluded area of Elysium, you stumble upon a small garden filled with cherry blossoms. Seated on a bench is a young woman, her face serene as she plucks the strings of a koto, a traditional instrument.
<>Greetings, traveler. I am Hana. Would you like to sit and listen? Music has a way of soothing even the most restless souls.<> <>I’d like that. It’s been a long journey.<> You sit beside Hana, letting the soft, melodic notes wash over you. The music is peaceful, almost hypnotic, and you feel a sense of calm settle over you. <>Music is a universal language, $name. It speaks to the heart, transcending all barriers.<> As you listen, you close your eyes, feeling the tension of your journey ease away. You thank Hana for the music and leave the garden, feeling refreshed and rejuvenated.

passages.name: mq24_day1
passages.source_raw:
<>You return to your ship, your heart pounding with anticipation. The piece of paper with the coordinates is clutched tightly in your hand. As you sit in the pilot's seat, you input the numbers Raphaella gave you, plotting the course towards the unknown destination. <>Coordinates are set... Let’s hope Raphaella wasn't lying.<> The ship hums to life, vibrating beneath your fingertips. The stars beyond the viewport begin to shift, aligning as the hyperdrive systems engage. You feel a sense of determination—no, something beyond determination, an obsession—to find your father. The vast emptiness of space has never felt so alive with possibilities. Your hand hovers over the console, then presses down on the button to initiate the hyperjump. The familiar sound of the engines ramping up fills the cabin, building into a powerful crescendo. You lean back in your seat, watching the stars streak past the viewport like trails of light in the darkness.
The ship vibrates intensely as it pushes through space at impossible speeds, the universe blurring around you. The hyperjump has begun, and you let out a slow breath, nerves momentarily settling. For just a second, you feel a fleeting sense of hope—perhaps you are finally on the right path, perhaps you are getting closer to him. <>Just hold on a little longer, Dad. I’m coming.<> But then, without warning, something shifts. The vibration changes. It becomes irregular. The engine's hum deepens into a growl, and a series of lights on the console blink red. You hear a high-pitched whine—the hyperdrive is straining. Suddenly, the ship jolts. You are thrown forward, barely managing to grab onto the console before the ship lurches violently. Warning lights flash, bathing the cabin in a pulsing red glow.
The alarm klaxons sound, echoing through the ship. Something has gone wrong, terribly wrong. The stars outside the viewport flicker, no longer streaking but instead swirling chaotically. Your ship is in danger, and so are you. <>No, no, no, this can’t be happening!<> You frantically scan the console for an answer, but the display is a blur of flashing symbols. Your mind races. You need to do something—fast. <> <>

passages.name: mq24_day1_2
passages.source_raw:
<>You are piloting your battered spaceship through a desolate sector of space. Alarms are blaring, and sparks fly from the control panel. <>Damn it! The hyperdrive is fried, and life support is failing. I need to find a place to land—fast!<> Through the viewport, a flickering light catches your eye—a small, isolated space gas station.
<>That’s my only hope.<> You steer the ship toward the station, and with a jolt, you dock at the derelict-looking facility. <><>

passages.name: Day2_Start
passages.source_raw:
<<narrator>>The mechanical hum of the station stirs you awake. Stretching, you recall the strange noises from the night before. 

You wake up in the dim quarters provided for you. The station's faint hum echoes through the walls, and for a moment, you let the silence linger. Remembering Gabbie's invitation, you stretch and prepare to head to the docking station.

<<speech $you "$name">>Gabbie said she'd need my help with the repairs today. I should go find her in the docking bay.<</speech>>

But as you stand, you notice how quiet the station seems. The memory of last night’s strange noises stirs a curiosity within you.

<<speech $you "$name">>Maybe I could take a quick look around first...<</speech>>

<<button [[Explore the station|Day2_ExploreStation]]>><<set $visitedStorage to false>><<set $visitedControlRoom to false>><<set $visitedCrewQuarters to false>><</button>><</narrator>>

passages.name: Day1_SilentStation
passages.source_raw:
<>You exit your ship into the dimly lit docking bay. The air is thick with the scent of oil and metal. Behind you, your mother and sister step down, looking around with a mix of exhaustion and curiosity. <>Hello? Is anyone here?<> Your voice echoes in the stillness. After a moment, a figure emerges from behind a stack of crates.
A young woman steps into the light, dressed in grease-streaked overalls and holding a wrench. Her eyes scan you warily, sizing you up. <>Didn’t expect company today. What’s your business here?<> <>My ship’s in bad shape. I need repairs, and fast.<> She glances at your ship, raising an eyebrow. <>Looks like you pushed her past her limits. Let me take a look.<> As she walks around your ship, inspecting the damage with a practiced eye, your mother, clearly fatigued from the journey, places a comforting hand on your sister’s shoulder. <>Honey, the jump took a lot out of us. Do you think there’s a place we could rest?<> Gabbie notices their weariness and nods, giving you a quick, understanding glance. <>They look like they could use a break. Head up the corridor, and you’ll meet Angel. She’ll set you up with a room to rest and something to eat.<> Your sister gives a small smile, her exhaustion evident. <>Thank you… We really appreciate it.<> <>You’re welcome. Angel is just down the hall; she’ll take care of you both.<> As they head off down the corridor, you feel a surge of relief, knowing they’ll be able to rest while you handle the repairs. <>Thank you. They’ve had a rough few days.<> Gabbie shrugs, leaning against your ship as she continues her inspection. <>I get it. And you’re lucky you made it here in one piece. Hyperdrive is shot, coolant leaks, and your nav systems are fried.<> <>How long to fix it?<> She sighs, crossing her arms. <>With the parts I have, maybe five days. But that’s working nonstop.<> <>I don’t have five days.<> She gives a slight smirk, arms still crossed. <>Well, unless you’ve got a magic wand, we’re stuck with reality. Welcome aboard, $name. I’m Gabbie, by the way.<> <>Glad to meet you, Gabbie.<> <> <>

passages.name: Day1_EmptyStation
passages.source_raw:
<>As she gathers tools, you glance around the station. <>This place is... quiet. Are you here alone?<> Gabbie pauses before answering. <>On the docking bay yes, most of the staff here are gone. There are other workers living here in the station though, but there are not many of us.<> <>Gone where?<> She shrugs. <>People come and go. Stations like this aren’t exactly bustling hubs.<> Her evasive answer piques your curiosity. While Gabbie starts on the repairs, you hear a faint clanking noise echoing from the station’s interior. <>Did you hear that?<> Gabbie doesn’t look up. <>Hear what?<> <>A noise. Like metal hitting metal.<> She tightens a bolt, her expression unchanged. <>Old station. Lots of noises. Nothing to worry about.<>
She continues examining and repairing your ship. After a while, Gabbie sets aside her tools. <>We should eat. Repairs will go smoother on a full stomach.<> <><>

passages.name: Day1_cantine
passages.source_raw:
<> You both walk over to the cantine, navigating through narrow, dimly lit hallways lined with exposed pipes and flickering lights. When you arrive, the cantine is a small, utilitarian room, its walls adorned with faded posters of distant planets and galaxies. A few tables are scattered around, occupied by a handful of tired-looking workers quietly eating their meals. The air smells of something warm and savory, though the underlying scent of recycled air persists.
A single worker, Elena, stands behind the counter, ladling portions of a thick, steaming stew into metal bowls. She looks up as you approach, giving Gabbie a faint, friendly nod. <>Hey, Elena. I’ll take the usual.<> Elena smiles knowingly and fills a bowl with the stew, then looks at you, raising an eyebrow in silent question.
<>I’ll have the same, thanks.<> Elena nods and fills a second bowl, sliding it across the counter to you. You and Gabbie take your trays and find a seat at an empty table near the wall. As you settle in, you take your first spoonful, finding the stew surprisingly comforting for something rehydrated. It’s warm, thick, and spiced just enough to mask the blandness typical of space meals. <>So, how many people live on this station?<> Gabbie takes a sip of her stew, glancing around the room before she answers. <>Not many these days. Most of the crew were reassigned or left over the years. There are a few of us who manage the place now – keeping things running, monitoring the systems, watching for any signs of… well, trouble.<> <>Sounds like it gets lonely.<> She shrugs. <>Sometimes. But it’s peaceful. Keeps me focused.<> You take another bite, the warmth of the meal slowly spreading through you. <>What is there to do here, then? Any hidden gems in this station?<> She chuckles softly. <>Not much in terms of entertainment. There’s the observation deck if you like staring into the void, a small gym for workouts, and the usual maintenance tasks. And there’s Elena’s cooking, of course. That’s about as exciting as it gets.<> <>Sounds… quiet.<> Gabbie smirks, taking a slow sip of her stew. <>Everyone’s just passing through.<>
You both share a brief smile, a shared understanding settling between you. The quiet, uneventful space of the station seems to be both a curse and a comfort to her. You sense there’s more to her story, but it doesn’t seem like she’s ready to share it all just yet. Instead, you chat about mundane topics—the quirks of long-haul travel, the odd things you’ve seen at various ports, and the humorous incidents that seem to come with the territory of spacefaring life. She listens intently, occasionally offering up her own stories, though you notice she avoids mentioning too much about her own past. After a while, Gabbie checks the time and stands, nodding toward the doorway. <>You’ll need somewhere to sleep tonight. Head over to see Angel down in the accommodation wing. Tell her I sent you, and she’ll find a room for you.<> You get up to follow her out of the cantine, your meal finished. As you reach the hallway, she turns to you, her expression a little softer. <>I’ll be in the docking bay tomorrow. Stop by when you’re ready, and we’ll see about getting your ship back in shape.<> <>Thanks, Gabbie. For everything.<> She gives a small, almost shy smile before turning to head in the opposite direction, disappearing down the corridor. <> <>

passages.name: Day1_Find_Angel
passages.source_raw:
<> Following Gabbie’s directions, you make your way through the station's narrow hallways toward the accommodation wing. The lighting is dim, casting long shadows across the corridor, and the occasional hum of machinery echoes in the distance. When you reach the designated area, you find a small office with a sign reading “Accommodations.” Inside, a woman with blonde hair is seated behind a cluttered desk, typing away on an old-fashioned console. She looks up as you approach, her bright blue eyes sparkling with a mischievous glint. She seems to be in her forties, with a smile that hints she’s no stranger to trouble.
<>Well, well, what do we have here? Another visitor? Gabbie didn’t tell me she was running a guesthouse!<> You offer a polite smile, not quite sure how to respond. <>Uh… Gabbie sent me. She said you’d have a room for me to stay in tonight.<> Angel raises an eyebrow, her grin widening. <>Oh, I figured as much. Already helped your $mom and $sis settle in earlier—poor things looked exhausted after that jump. Now, let’s see if we can’t find you a place to rest too.<> Her tone shifts to something more playful as she leans back, appraising you with a teasing look. <>So, how’d you two meet? You and Gabbie…<> <>I, uh, had a bit of trouble with my ship. Docked here for repairs.<> Angel smirks, clearly amused by your awkwardness. <>And here I thought she’d finally decided to bring home a boyfriend. Shame.<> You chuckle, trying to match her playful energy. <>Just a pilot in need of a repair, nothing more.<> She leans forward, her voice dropping to a conspiratorial whisper. <>Well, sugar, I’m not usually one to miss an opportunity. If you’re only here for a short stay, I’d better make the most of it, hmm?<> Her tone is teasing, and you can’t help but grin, realizing she’s just having a bit of harmless fun. <>I’ll be out of your hair as soon as my ship’s fixed. But I appreciate the… warm welcome.<> Angel laughs, a rich, hearty sound that echoes through the small office. <>Oh, sweetheart, I’ll take any excuse to entertain a handsome visitor like you. You sure you don’t want to stay a little longer?<> You shake your head, trying not to laugh at her audacious charm. <>Tempting offer, but I’ve got a mission to get back to.<> She sighs theatrically, placing a hand over her heart. <>Ah, the good ones are always on some grand adventure. Well, let me grab you a key before I decide to steal you away myself.<> She gets up, rummaging through a drawer and producing a small metal key with a number etched on it. She hands it to you, a playful smile still dancing on her lips. <>Room 12, just down the hall. Sheets are clean, bed’s as comfortable as it gets out here. Now, don’t let Gabbie keep you all to herself, okay? You come see me if you need anything… anything at all.<> You nod, chuckling as you pocket the key. <>Thanks, Angel. I’ll keep that in mind.<> She gives you a final wink before turning back to her console, clearly satisfied with having flustered you a bit.
With the key in hand and a smile on your face, you head toward your quarters, already looking forward to what tomorrow might bring. <> <>

passages.name: Day1_Room
passages.source_raw:
<> You find Room 12 at the end of a narrow hallway, its walls lined with faded posters and dented metal panels. Unlocking the door with the key Angel provided, you step into a small, dimly lit room. It’s sparse but functional: a narrow bunk built into the wall, a small desk with an outdated terminal, and a shelf containing a few essentials like towels and a small first aid kit. A single viewport offers a glimpse of the endless stars outside, casting a faint, bluish glow across the room. The recycled air hums through the vents, giving the place a stale but oddly comforting feel. You sit on the edge of the bunk, the mattress firm but surprisingly comfortable.
As you lie back, the events of the day begin to play through your mind. Meeting Gabbie, navigating her evasive answers, and the strange, lonely aura of this station all leave you feeling both curious and wary. Suddenly, a dull, distant thud reverberates through the walls, interrupting your thoughts. The noise is faint, yet unmistakable in the silence of the room. <>What is going on here?<> You sit up, listening intently, but the sound does not repeat. You remember Gabbie’s earlier dismissal when you heard something strange before, and you decide to let it go for now. The last thing you want is to break any unspoken rules in this unfamiliar place. Sighing, you lie back down, staring at the metallic ceiling. A hundred questions circle in your mind, none with easy answers. <>She’s hiding something. But then again, so am I.<> You think back to your fleeting conversations with Gabbie—the glimpses of warmth in her guarded demeanor, her willingness to help with your ship, her hints of a past she keeps closely guarded. In many ways, she’s as much a mystery as this station. And yet, you feel drawn to her, sensing a connection beyond mere circumstance. As your thoughts drift, the hum of the station’s systems becomes a rhythmic lullaby. Your eyelids grow heavy, and the day’s fatigue finally begins to overtake you. A faint whisper seems to echo through the silence—a trick of the mind, perhaps, or maybe another residual noise from the station’s aging systems. You try to shake it off, but a feeling of unease lingers. Despite it, sleep finally claims you, the mysteries of the station waiting patiently for you in the morning. <><>
