passages.name: Day2_CrewQuarters
passages.source_raw: <> <>You enter the Crew Quarters, a section of the station that’s both functional and oddly homey, with personal items scattered around—a few jackets hanging on hooks, some graffiti on the walls, and a faded poster or two. The air here feels a bit warmer, less sterile than the rest of the station. As you turn a corner, you spot Angel—the blonde woman who assigned you your room. She’s leaning casually against the wall, arms crossed and a smirk already forming on her face as she notices you. <>Well, well. Look who decided to stop by. Couldn’t stay away from me, huh?<> Her voice is teasing, her eyes glinting with that mischievous look you’re beginning to associate with her. You chuckle, feeling a bit of warmth at her familiarity in this otherwise cold station. <>What can I say? Your charm is irresistible.<> You offer a playful wink, which only widens Angel's smirk. She pushes off the wall and takes a step closer, making the narrow corridor feel even more intimate. <>Flattery will get you everywhere, sugar. So, how'd you sleep? Bed comfortable enough for you?<> There’s a suggestive undertone to her question that you can’t miss. You feel a flush of heat creep up your neck. <>It was… adequate, though I’ll admit, it felt a bit empty.<> Angel’s eyes light up at your response, clearly pleased that you’re playing along. <>Oh? Well, we can’t have that, can we?<> She leans in just a little closer, her perfume a subtle, intoxicating scent. <>You know, I could always give you the special, VIP, relaxing treatment... you know... right here, right know.<> Her hand brushes your arm, and you’re momentarily caught off guard by her warmth and closeness. <>I… uh… that sounds…<> You stammer, trying to keep your composure under her mischievous gaze. Angel chuckles, a low, throaty sound that sends a shiver down your spine. <>Relax, sugar. I don't bite... unless you want me to.<> \ <>\ <><> <>\ <><> <>

passages.name: Day2_DockingStation
passages.source_raw:
<<narrator>>Determined to find answers, you make your way to the docking bay.

Gabbie is already there, tinkering with a console, her back turned to you.

<<speech $you "$name">>Morning, Gabbie.<</speech>>

She glances over her shoulder, offering a faint smile.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>Morning. Sleep well?<</speech>>

<<speech $you "$name">>Well enough. Ready to tackle more repairs?<</speech>>

She nods, wiping her hands on a rag.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>I’ve mapped out what needs to be done today. Could use an extra set of hands.<</speech>>

You notice dark circles under her eyes.

<<speech $you "$name">>You okay? You look tired.<</speech>>

She avoids your gaze.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>Just stayed up late running diagnostics. Let’s get started.<</speech>>

<<button [[Continue|Day2_CollaborativeRepairs]]>><</button>><</narrator>>

passages.name: Day2_Cafeteria
passages.source_raw:
<> <> You enter the cafeteria, greeted by the faint aroma of synthetic coffee and the hum of low conversations. You head to the dispenser, fill a cup with the steaming, dark liquid, and find an empty seat near a small group of crew members talking in hushed tones.
As you take a sip of the coffee—bitter and metallic, but oddly comforting—you catch snippets of their conversation about strange noises in the corridors and something about an "incident" in the storage bay. \ <> <><> <> <><> <>

passages.name: Day2_GameRoom
passages.source_raw:
<><>You step into the Game Room, greeted by the glow of neon lights and the low hum of arcade machines. The walls are lined with various game consoles and virtual reality setups, though most of the machines stand idle, casting colorful reflections on the floor. Despite the empty feel, the room has an inviting atmosphere. Across the room, you spot Skylar, a lively woman with an easy smile and a confident air. She’s adjusting the settings on one of the VR consoles but looks up when you enter, waving you over.
<>Hey there! Looking for a bit of fun? I can show you around the VR setup, or maybe we could have a little competition. What do you think?<> You return her smile and chat briefly, talking about the station and how you ended up here. When she asks what you’re doing in a place like this, you explain that you’re only here until Gabbie finishes the repairs on your ship. <>I’m hoping to get back out there soon—just waiting on Gabbie to work her magic on my ship.<> Skylar chuckles, crossing her arms with an appreciative nod. <>Then you’ll be out of here in no time. Gabbie’s the best there is. She manages the whole repair dock by herself, and somehow, nothing gets past her.<> Curious, you ask about her role on the station, and she shrugs, looking around the empty game room with a slightly wistful expression. <>Me? I was sent here by my company to run this game room. It was meant to be a place for the crew to unwind, you know? But with the station being practically empty these days…<> She trails off, her smile turning a bit wry. <>Honestly, I think they’ll close this place up soon. Not much point in keeping it open when there’s hardly anyone around.<> You nod, understanding the situation. Despite the station’s emptiness, there’s something charming about her presence here, holding down this corner of entertainment in an otherwise quiet outpost. <>Well, it’s been nice getting to know you, Skylar. I should probably head over to the dockyard, though.<> She grins, the spark returning to her eyes as she raises an eyebrow. <>You better come back tomorrow. I’ll set up a few games for us—could be a nice distraction from this ghost town of a station.<> You laugh, appreciating the invitation. There’s something refreshing about her easygoing nature in this otherwise desolate place. <>Maybe sticking around a bit longer won’t be so bad.<> With a friendly nod, you take one last look around the Game Room before heading out, already planning to return for some games with Skylar. <> <>

passages.name: Day2_ObservationDeck
passages.source_raw:
<> <>You and your $mom step into the Observation Deck, a quiet, dimly lit space with floor-to-ceiling windows that open out to the vast expanse of stars. The view is breathtaking, with countless stars shimmering against the deep black of space, and a distant nebula casting a faint, colorful glow.
You both take a seat by the window, letting the peaceful scene wash over you. For a moment, it’s easy to lose yourself in the beauty of the cosmos, but your thoughts soon drift back to your mission. Your $mom seems to notice the shift in your expression. <>I know that look. You’re thinking about him, aren’t you?<> You nod, glancing over at her. The weight of your responsibility feels a little lighter with her beside you, sharing this quiet moment. <>I have to get back to the plan. Dad… wherever he is, he doesn’t have time to waste. If Gabbie can get those repairs done quickly, I might still be able to get back on track and find him before it’s too late.<> Your mother sighs softly, her gaze fixed on the stars beyond the glass. <>Your father always had a way of getting into trouble, didn’t he? But I know you’ll do everything you can to bring him home.<> The memory of your last conversation with him comes flooding back—his voice, urging you to stay strong, to keep going, no matter the odds. You wonder where he is now and what he’s enduring. Your $mom seems lost in her own thoughts, a trace of worry lining her face. <>Hold on, Dad. I’m coming. I just need this station—and these repairs—to cooperate.<> You lean forward, pressing a hand against the glass, as if somehow the stars might hold the answer. Your $mom reaches out, placing a gentle hand on your shoulder, offering silent support. <>We’ll get through this together, $name. Whatever it takes, we’ll bring him back.<> Lost in your thoughts, you take a deep breath, feeling both the weight of your responsibility and the determination pushing you forward. This mission is all that matters.
Suddenly, a glimmer outside the window catches both of your eyes—a faint flash, too fast to fully register, disappearing just as quickly. Your $mom ’s eyes widen slightly, as if sharing your sense of wonder. <>The universe always seems to have a way of reminding us that we’re never truly alone, doesn’t it?<> You nod, finding comfort in her words and the silent beauty of the stars stretching out before you. <> <>

passages.name: Day2_Library
passages.source_raw:
<> <>You and your $sis step into the quiet Library & Archives, where rows of shelves are filled with old Federation records, data archives, and dusty books. The soft hum of the station’s systems is barely audible here, lending a peaceful, almost timeless feel to the space. Your $sis ’s eyes widen as she takes in the shelves, clearly impressed. <>Wow, I didn’t expect to see a place like this out here… it’s like stepping into a forgotten corner of the universe.<> At a nearby table, a middle-aged man with graying hair and a calm, thoughtful expression is cataloging files. He looks up as you both enter, his gaze sharp but welcoming.
<>Ah, two new faces. We don’t get many visitors here, especially curious ones. Looking for something specific?<> You introduce yourself and your $sis, mentioning your curiosity about the station’s history. Tariq nods, placing the stack of records aside as he leans back thoughtfully. <>This station? It wasn’t always so quiet. There was a time when it was bustling with traders, explorers, and cargo ships from all over. This place was a vital stop in the galaxy—a hub of commerce, stories, and opportunity.<> He sighs, a trace of nostalgia in his eyes. <>But that was before the Federation pulled out. They abandoned this sector, saying it wasn’t worth protecting anymore. Without their patrols, pirates moved in. These routes became dangerous, especially for civilians. Now, hardly anyone stops here unless they have no other choice.<> You nod, absorbing his words as the station’s emptiness begins to make more sense—a relic, a shadow of its former self, left to survive on the outskirts of Federation care. <>That’s so sad. It must have been incredible back in the day, with people from all over passing through.<> Tariq glances at her with a sympathetic smile. <>Yes, it was. Nowadays, the only people who come by are those who, like me, don’t have any other choice. Some of us need a place to rest, others need repairs, and a few… well, they’re just hiding from something out there.<> He gestures toward the shelves, his gaze drifting over the collection of books. <>Despite everything, there’s something special here. These archives hold records from the old days, before the Federation stretched its reach this far. Pre-Federation books, philosophies, stories from forgotten worlds—things you won’t find in many places these days.<> You walk over to the shelves he indicated, scanning the spines of books with titles worn by time. Some of them bear the marks of distant worlds, written in languages long forgotten by most. Your sister reaches out, running her fingers over the faded lettering on one of the books, clearly fascinated. <>This place is a treasure trove… I didn’t think places like this still existed.<> You’re struck by the richness of this collection—a hidden trove of knowledge and culture from a time before the Federation’s dominance. <>Pre-Federation books… There’s so much history here, hidden away in this quiet corner of space. I’ll definitely need to come back and explore this more.<> Turning back to Tariq, you thank him for the insight, mentioning that you’ll both return soon to look through the collection in more detail. He nods, a faint smile on his face. <>You’re welcome anytime. It’s good to see people who appreciate what this place has to offer.<> With one last look at the shelves, you and your sister leave the Library & Archives, already planning to return and delve deeper into the forgotten knowledge it holds. <> <>

passages.name: Day2_MedicalBay
passages.source_raw:
<> <> You enter the Medical Bay, where the sterile scent of antiseptic fills the air. Various medical equipment lines the walls, and Doctor Reeva—a tall, sharp-eyed woman with a no-nonsense expression—is organizing supplies at a nearby counter.
She notices you and waves you over. <>Ah, the new arrival. Here for a check-up, I assume? Don’t worry; I don’t bite.<> She gestures for you to sit on an examination bed, grabbing a handheld scanner and some basic diagnostic tools. <>Let’s get this over with. Just a quick scan to make sure you’re adapting to the station’s artificial environment.<> Doctor Reeva moves the scanner over you, her expression focused as she checks the device's readings. After a moment, she raises an eyebrow and smirks. <>Looks like you're in perfect health. No signs of radiation exposure, no elevated stress hormones… Guess you haven’t spent enough time on this station to get affected by the ‘strange happenings’ everyone’s always whispering about.<> \ <>\ <><> <>\ <><> <>

passages.name: Day2_CollaborativeRepairs
passages.source_raw:
<<narrator>><<speech $you "$name">>I’ve got it.<</speech>>

She watches as you work, a hint of approval in her eyes.

During a short break, you strike up a conversation.

<<speech $you "$name">>So, how did you end up on this station working all alone?<</speech>>

She hesitates before replying.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>It’s a long story. Let’s just say I prefer solitude.<</speech>>

<<speech $you "$name">>And here I thought you were enjoying my company.<</speech>>

She chuckles softly.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>You’re not the worst company I’ve had.<</speech>>

You spend the morning working side by side, the silence filled only by the sounds of tools and machinery.

At one point, Gabbie hands you a plasma torch.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>Careful with this. We need to re-weld the conduit casing. Steady hands.<</speech>>

You take the torch, your fingers brushing hers briefly. You both continue working for a while until Gabbie breaks the silence to ask you:

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>Hey, can you bring me a hydro-spanner from the storage room? It’s down the corridor, third door on the left.<</speech>>

<<button [[Continue|Day2_LockedDoor]]>><</button>><</narrator>>

passages.name: Day2_LockedDoor
passages.source_raw:
<>Gabbie sends you to fetch a hydro-spanner from Storage Room B. As you navigate the dim hallway, you hear that faint, rhythmic tapping again. You follow the sound to a heavy, locked door with a faded sign: “Authorized Personnel Only.” <>What’s behind here?<> You lean in, trying to discern the source of the noise. Suddenly, Gabbie’s voice cuts through the silence. <>I thought I told you to go to Storage Room B.<>
You turn to see her standing behind you, arms crossed. <>I heard something... thought it might be important.<> Her eyes narrow. <>This area’s off-limits. Let’s stick to where you need to be.<> <>If there’s something wrong with the station, I think I have a right to know.<> She steps closer, her tone softening slightly. <>Trust me, it’s nothing you need to worry about. Come on, I already grabbed the thing.<> <> <>

passages.name: Day2_TensionRising
passages.source_raw:
<<narrator>>Back at the docking bay, the atmosphere is strained. You decide to break the silence.

<<speech $you "$name">>Look, I’m not trying to pry, but if there’s a problem—<</speech>>

She interrupts.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>Drop it, okay? Focus on getting your ship fixed.<</speech>>

You bite back a retort, sensing that pushing further won’t help. Your thoughts drift to your father, and the urgency of your mission. You both continue working in silence for a while.

...

Gabbie approaches quietly, standing beside you.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>I owe you an apology.<</speech>>

You glance at her, surprised.

<<speech $you "$name">>For what?<</speech>>

She sighs.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>For snapping at you earlier. This place... it gets to me sometimes.<</speech>>

<<speech $you "$name">>It’s okay. We’re both under stress.<</speech>>

She offers a tentative smile.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>Truce?<</speech>>

<<speech $you "$name">>Truce.<</speech>>

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>Great, let's get something to eat. I can't work with an empty stomach.<</speech>>

<<button [[Continue|Day2_SharedStories]]>><</button>>

<</narrator>>

passages.name: Day2_SharedStories
passages.source_raw:
<<narrator>>You both walk together through the station towards the cantine.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>So, tell me about your father.<</speech>>

You pause, considering how much to reveal.

<<speech $you "$name">>He’s... well, he’s everything to me. The federation took him because he knew things they wanted to keep quiet.<</speech>>

She nods, empathy in her eyes.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>The federation has a way of tearing families apart.<</speech>>

<<speech $you "$name">>Did they... did they take someone from you too?<</speech>>

She looks away.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>In a manner of speaking.<</speech>>

<<button [[Arrive at the cantine|Day2_EveningMeal]]>><</button>><</narrator>>

passages.name: Day2_EveningMeal
passages.source_raw:
<>You head to the cantine for dinner. A few tired-looking workers sit scattered across the tables, eating quietly, the hum of the station ever-present in the background. At the counter, Elena is ladling portions of a thick, steaming stew into metal bowls. She looks up as you and Gabbie approach, giving her a faint, friendly nod. <>Hey, Elena. We’ll take two bowls of the usual.<> Elena nods, filling two bowls with the stew and sliding them across the counter to you. You both take your trays and find a seat at a nearby table. The stew is warm and hearty, its earthy aroma filling the air around you. As you take your first bite, you find it surprisingly comforting for station food, the spices masking any hint of blandness. Gabbie stirs her stew thoughtfully, glancing around the room before meeting your eyes.
<>So, want to expand on your story? I'm quite curious, you are a very talented mechanic...<> She sighs, setting her spoon down momentarily as if deciding how much to share. <>I used to work on a cargo ship. We’d run supplies between stations, transport goods to the outer colonies. It wasn’t glamorous, but it was freedom. There’s something about life on a ship—moving through the stars, the thrill of new places… It felt like home.<> She pauses, a distant look crossing her face. You can tell there’s more to the story, so you wait patiently, giving her space to continue. <>What happened?<> She stirs her stew, the spoon moving slowly, almost absently. <>We got caught in a Federation skirmish. Pirates had been raiding the sector, and the Federation decided to clean them out. They swept in without much regard for who else was there. We were in the wrong place at the wrong time.<> Her voice tightens slightly, and she takes a breath, steadying herself. <>We lost some good people that day. People who didn’t deserve it. The Federation called it collateral damage, but it felt like they were too quick to write us off.<> You offer a sympathetic nod, understanding the weight of her words. <>I’m sorry, Gabbie. That’s… hard to come back from.<> She gives a small, sad smile, her gaze softening a bit. <>Thanks. But out here, that’s just life. You lose people, you keep going. There’s no time for regrets in space. Just… memories.<> The two of you fall into a comfortable silence, the quiet clinking of cutlery around the room providing a steady rhythm. You take another bite, the warmth of the meal slowly easing the weight of the conversation. After a moment, you glance over, curious about what drew her to the station. <>So, after that, you decided to stay here?<> She chuckles softly, a touch of irony in her expression. <>More like I didn’t have many options left. Crews don’t usually line up to hire people who come from ships that don’t make it back. So I took the first stable job I could find. Maintenance, repairs… turns out I’m pretty good at it.<> Her gaze drifts around the cantine, taking in the quiet figures and the worn walls, a place she’s clearly grown used to. <>This place isn’t much, but at least it’s steady. I can fix things, keep the station running, and sometimes, that’s all you really need.<> You nod, admiring her resilience. <>Not everyone could keep going after something like that. You’ve found your way, even if it’s not the way you planned.<> She offers a genuine smile this time, a softness in her eyes that wasn’t there before. <>Thanks. I guess you’re right. Sometimes, it’s the little things that keep you going. A quiet station, a good repair job, and maybe some decent company once in a while.<> The two of you continue eating in silence, sharing a quiet camaraderie that feels natural, almost comforting. You talk a bit about the station—its quirks, the strange things you’ve both encountered in your travels. Gabbie listens intently, and occasionally she offers her own stories, though you notice she still holds back on certain details, keeping parts of herself guarded. After a while, Gabbie glances at the time, finishing off the last of her stew. She stands and nods toward the doorway. <>I’ll be in the docking bay tomorrow. Stop by when you’re ready, and we’ll see about getting your ship back in shape.<> You rise as well, feeling a sense of connection with her that you hadn’t expected. <>Thanks, Gabbie. For the company—and the conversation.<> She gives a small, almost shy smile before turning to head off down the corridor. <> <>

passages.name: Day2_NightWhispers
passages.source_raw:
<<narrator>>Later that night, you lie awake, the station’s silence unsettling. The whispers begin again, barely audible.

<<speech $you "$name">>There it is again.<</speech>>

Determined, you decide to investigate despite Gabbie’s warning.

<<button [[Continue|Day2_FollowVoices]]>><</button>><</narrator>>

passages.name: Day2_FollowVoices
passages.source_raw:
<>You follow the ethereal sounds through winding corridors, the whispers growing louder yet remaining indistinct. They lead you once more to the locked door. This time, you notice a keypad.
<>If only I could figure out the code.<> As you contemplate your next move, a shadow falls over you. Gabbie stands behind you, a mix of concern and frustration on her face.
<>You just couldn’t let it go, could you?<> <>I need to know what’s going on. Those whispers... it’s like someone is calling out.<> She steps closer, her voice barely above a whisper. <>Please. For your own safety, stay away from this door.<> <>Then help me understand. What’s behind it?<> She closes her eyes, conflicted. <>It’s... a part of my past I’d rather forget. But maybe you deserve to know.<> She looks around, ensuring you’re alone. <>Meet me in the control room tomorrow morning. I’ll explain everything.<> <>Alright. I appreciate it.<> She turns to leave but pauses. <>And please, don’t wander the halls alone at night. It’s not safe.<> With that, she disappears into the shadows. <><>

passages.name: Day2_Quarters
passages.source_raw:
<<narrator>>Back in your room, you reflect on the day’s events.

<<speech $you "$name">>She’s hiding something big. But at least she’s willing to talk now.<</speech>>

Exhaustion finally takes over as you drift into a restless sleep.

<<button [[Fall asleep|Day2_sleeping]]>><</button>><</narrator>>

passages.name: Day2_sleeping
passages.source_raw:
<>You decide to go to sleep for the day.
\ <> \<><><><> <> \<><> <>

passages.name: Day3_Start
passages.source_raw:
<<narrator>>The steady hum of the station stirs you awake, the soft vibration of machinery a reminder of your current home away from home. Stretching, you take a moment to collect your thoughts, memories of the previous day and night drifting back to you.

You recall Gabbie’s invitation to continue working on the repairs today, and a slight feeling of anticipation nudges you as you prepare to face whatever the day holds.

<<speech $you "$name">>Time to explore the station a bit more… and hopefully make some headway on those repairs.<</speech>>

You quickly get ready, mentally listing the places you want to go. There's the Game Room, Cafeteria, Medical Bay, and Crew Quarters to check out. Once you've had your fill of wandering, you'll meet Gabbie in the Docking Station.

<<button [[Head to the hallway|Day3_Hallway]]>><</button>>
<</narrator>>

passages.name: Day3_Hallway
passages.source_raw:
<<narrator>>
You step into the main hallway of the station, surrounded by dimly lit corridors branching out to different parts of the facility. You take a moment to plan your route—there’s the Game Room, Cafeteria, Medical Bay, and Crew Quarters you could visit before heading back to the Docking Station to meet Gabbie.

<<if !$visitedGameRoom_Day3>>
  <<button [[Visit the Game Room|Day3_GameRoom]]>><</button>><<else>><<disable>>@@.dis;<<button "Visit the Game Room" disabled>><</button>>@@<</disable>><</if>>

<<if !$visitedCafeteria_Day3>>
  <<button [[Go to the Cafeteria|Day3_Cafeteria]]>><</button>><<else>><<disable>>@@.dis;<<button "Go to the Cafeteria" disabled>><</button>>@@<</disable>><</if>>

<<if !$visitedCrewQuarters_Day3>>
  <<button [[Visit the Crew Quarters|Day3_CrewQuarters]]>><</button>><<else>><<disable>>@@.dis;<<button "Visit the Crew Quarters" disabled>><</button>>@@<</disable>><</if>>

<<if $visitedGameRoom_Day3 and $visitedCafeteria_Day3 and $visitedCrewQuarters_Day3>>
  <<button [[Go to the Docking Station|Day3_DockingStation]]>><</button>><<else>>Explore the station first!<<disable>>@@.dis;<<button "Go to the Docking Station" disabled>><</button>>@@<</disable>><</if>>
<</narrator>>

passages.name: Day3_GameRoom
passages.source_raw:
<><>You step into the Game Room, the neon lights casting their familiar glow on the rows of consoles and VR setups. Across the room, Skylar is waiting for you, a grin spreading across her face as she waves you over. <>Hey! I set up one of the racing simulators just for us. I hope you’re ready to lose!<> You can’t help but chuckle at her playful challenge as you settle into the racing machine beside her. She taps a few buttons, and the virtual race begins. The controls are responsive, the simulation surprisingly immersive, and you find yourself caught up in the excitement as you and Skylar race through twisting tracks and sharp turns.
After a close competition, the race finishes with a narrow win—though you’re both laughing and breathless from the intensity. Skylar steps out of the simulator, her face flushed with excitement. <>Wow… I haven’t had that much fun in ages.<> She glances at you, a bit nervously, tucking a stray piece of hair behind her ear. <>Thank you. Really.<>
\ <>\ <><> <>\ <><> <>

passages.name: Day3_Cafeteria
passages.source_raw:
<><>You make your way to the cafeteria, hoping to grab a quick cup of coffee to start the day. When you arrive, you find the space completely empty—the quiet only broken by the faint hum of the station’s machinery. You head over to the coffee dispenser, filling a cup with the dark, steaming liquid. The familiar, slightly metallic aroma fills the air as you take a sip. It’s strong and bitter, but it does the job, giving you the energy boost you need.
With no one around to talk to, you finish your coffee quickly, setting the empty cup aside before heading back out. <> <>

passages.name: Day3_CrewQuarters
passages.source_raw:
<<set $visitedCrewQuarters_Day3 to true>><<narrator>>You make your way to the Crew Quarters, the thought of seeing Angel again adding a bit of anticipation to your steps. The area is quiet, the familiar sights of personal items scattered around and the faint, lingering scent of her perfume from yesterday bringing a faint smile to your face.

However, as you look around, you realize Angel isn’t here. Your gaze drifts across the room until you spot a small note left on one of the tables. Curious, you walk over and pick it up, instantly recognizing her neat handwriting.

<<speech "note" "Note">>$name, I knew you would come by looking for me. I got a busy day, maybe one of these nights I'll drop by your quarters if you remember to leave the door unlocked... xoxo<</speech>>

You can’t help but grin as you read her message, the playful tone unmistakably hers. The idea of her stopping by later lingers in your mind, making you wanting to go on about your day quickly.

With a last look around, you tuck the note away and turn to leave.

<<button [[Return to the Hall|Day3_Hallway]]>><</button>>

<</narrator>>

passages.name: Day3_DockingStation
passages.source_raw:
<>You walk up to the docking bay with sense of anticipation. Gabbie promised to reveal the secrets she's been keeping. Making your way to the control room, you find her already there, surrounded by flickering monitors displaying streams of data. <>Morning, Gabbie.<>
She turns to you, her expression serious. <>Morning. I'm glad you came.<> She gestures to a chair beside her. <>Have a seat. There's a lot we need to cover.<> Gabbie brings up a holographic display showing encrypted communications. <>I've been intercepting federation transmissions for months. They're working on a project called 'Echo.' It's... not good.<> <>What does this have to do with me?<> She hesitates before continuing. <>Your father's involved. He's being held at a black site, and they're using him to advance their agenda.<> <>You knew about my father?<> She nods. <>I recognized your ship's signature. I've been monitoring any activity related to 'Echo.' When you showed up, I realized it wasn't a coincidence.<> <>So you've been spying on me?<> She meets your gaze steadily. <>I had to be sure of your intentions. The federation has spies everywhere.<> <>And what about you? How do I know you're not one of them?<> She sighs, rubbing her temples. <>Because I was one of them. But not anymore.<> She takes a deep breath, her voice tinged with regret. <>I was a technician working on Project Echo. At first, I thought it was for the greater good. But when I saw what they were doing—experimenting on innocent people—I couldn't be a part of it.<> You study her, the pieces starting to fit together. <>So you ran.<> <>Yes. I escaped and came here, using this station to monitor their activities, hoping to find a way to stop them.<> You feel your anger subsiding, replaced by empathy. <>I want to rescue my father. Maybe we can help each other.<> She looks at you, hope flickering in her eyes. <>I was thinking the same. With your ship and my intel, we might have a chance.<> She stands up, motioning for you to follow. <>There's something you need to see.<> <><>

passages.name: Day3_Locked
passages.source_raw:
<>She leads you back to the locked door. Entering a code on the keypad, the door slides open with a hiss. Inside, the room is filled with advanced equipment—servers humming, screens displaying various data feeds, and a central holographic projector.
<>This is... impressive.<> <>I've been gathering as much information as I can. Here—<> She pulls up a file, displaying your father's image along with schematics and coordinates. <>This is the black site where they're keeping him.<> <>We need to act fast.<> She nods. <>Agreed. But first, we need to finish repairing your ship and make some modifications to evade their sensors.<> <>I appreciate your help, Gabbie.<> She smiles faintly. <>We're in this together now.<> <>I'm glad. Let's get to work then.<> <><>

passages.name: Day3_RepairMontage
passages.source_raw:
<<narrator>>After a grueling stretch of repairs, you and Gabbie take a short break, finding a moment of calm amidst the hum of machinery. The station feels quieter than usual, as though it, too, is catching its breath.

<<speech $you "$name">>You know, for someone who claims to prefer solitude, you're surprisingly good company.<</speech>>

She laughs softly, the sound catching you off guard with its warmth.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>Don’t get too comfortable. I’m still not one for crowds.<</speech>>

You both share a chuckle, and the tension that’s been hanging between you eases, replaced by a quiet sense of camaraderie. As Gabbie returns to adjust some settings on a terminal, you notice a screen flashing with partially decrypted messages. Intrigued, you glance over the text and catch phrases like "Project Echo" and "neural conditioning."

<<thought $you "$name">>Maybe this is my chance to find out what they’re really hiding here.<</thought>>

You scroll quickly, skimming through disturbing reports—mentioning experiments with mind control and attempts to merge artificial intelligence with human consciousness. As the weight of the implications sink in, Gabbie catches you reading.

<<speech "gabbie" "Gabbie">>Hey! What are you doing?<</speech>>

passages.name: Day5_Cafeteria
passages.source_raw:
<><>As you enter the cafeteria, you spot your $mom and $sis seated at a corner table, sharing a quiet breakfast. They look up as you approach, and a faint smile lights up your $mom’s face, though you can see a hint of worry in her eyes. <>Good morning, honey. Did you get any sleep? You’ve been working so hard lately.<> You give her a reassuring nod, pulling up a chair beside them. <>I did. And I’ve got some news. The ship is almost done—it’ll be ready by the end of the day. But… there’s something I need to tell you both.<> Your $sis glances up, her face lighting up with a mix of excitement and concern. <>So we’re finally going to find him? You’re taking us along, right?<> You take a deep breath, choosing your words carefully. <>The ship will be ready, but… you’re not coming with me. I need you both to stay here, where you’ll be safe. This part—I have to do it alone.<> A worried look flashes across your $mom’s face, and she sits up straighter. <>No. Absolutely not. We’ve waited all this time, we’ve come all this way together—I can’t just let you go off on your own like this. You’ll need us there, $name.<> <>$mom, please. This is what Dad asked of me—to come alone. I have to be cautious. If I don’t comply, there’s a chance the Federation will intervene, and I don’t want to risk putting you both in harm’s way.<> You reach across the table, resting a hand on hers. <>And someone has to look out for $name_sis if anything happens. Here, you’ll be safer. And I need you both to trust me on this.<> A heavy silence settles between you, and your $mom looks down, her hands clasped tightly. <>You’re asking me to do the one thing I never wanted to—watch you go off alone, just like your father did. I can’t bear the thought of losing you both.<> <>I know. But I promise you, I’ll come back. I’ll come back for you both—with or without him. I’m not going to abandon you. I’m the man of the house now, and this is my responsibility to prove it.<> Your words seem to sink in, and $sis leans forward, wrapping her arms around you tightly.
<>I know you will, $name. I believe in you.<> Your $mom watches you both for a moment, then her face softens as she pulls you into a hug as well, her grip strong and full of unspoken words. <>Just… promise me. Promise me you’ll come back, $name.<>
You nod, a swell of determination rising within you. <>I promise, $mom. No matter what happens, don’t lose hope. We’re in this together, even if I have to be the one out there fighting for us.<> The three of you share a quiet moment, holding onto each other as if trying to memorize this feeling, this promise. <> <>

passages.name: Day5_DockingStation
passages.source_raw:
<>You make your way to the docking bay, feeling a mixture of anticipation and determination. The ship stands before you, its repairs almost complete, and you feel a surge of gratitude for Gabbie’s help over the past few days. As you approach, you see Gabbie already hard at work on the ship’s final adjustments, her face focused yet subtly tense.
She glances at you briefly as you join her, and though you both exchange a small nod, there’s an unspoken tension hanging in the air. The memory of last night’s kiss lingers, and you can’t help but wonder if she’s thinking about it too. <>Let’s finish this up.<> She nods, handing you a tool and pointing out a few final adjustments that need attention. The two of you work in comfortable silence, each absorbed in your task, though you can feel her gaze lingering on you from time to time. It’s subtle, but there’s a new, nervous energy around her—a vulnerability that wasn’t there before. <>She’s nervous. Maybe it’s about the kiss... or maybe she’s worried about what’s to come.<> Minutes stretch into an hour as you both continue to work side by side, meticulously checking every detail. Finally, you secure the last panel, stepping back to survey your work. The ship gleams under the docking bay lights, its exterior whole once again. The repairs are complete. You turn to Gabbie, ready to thank her, but she’s already looking at you, her expression both hesitant and resolute. <>$name, I want to talk to you...<> You pause, the weight of her tone catching you off guard. She takes a step closer, her gaze intense as she seems to gather her thoughts. <> <>

passages.name: Day5_GabbieTalk
passages.source_raw:
<>Gabbie takes a steadying breath, her eyes meeting yours with an intensity you haven’t seen before.
<>$name... I didn’t come to this station to fix ships and live in solitude because I wanted to. After... everything that happened, I thought isolating myself was the best way to protect myself. This station became a place where I could just... disappear.<> She hesitates, her voice growing softer. <>I never thought anyone would come along who could... make me feel hope again. But then you showed up, with your determination and your loyalty. You reminded me that maybe I don’t have to be alone.<> She takes a step closer, her hand reaching for yours. <>I just want you to know... I’m thankful for everything. For showing me that it’s okay to feel, to believe in something beyond just surviving.<> Without another word, she leans in, pressing her lips to yours in a deep, passionate kiss. You feel the warmth and intensity of her emotions, and you respond, pulling her closer and letting the moment envelop you both. Her arms wrap around you, and the two of you stand there, locked in an embrace that speaks to everything you’ve both left unsaid.
As your hands drift along her back, a surge of desire rises within you, and you make a gentle move to draw her even closer. But Gabbie pulls back slightly, her gaze holding a mixture of longing and restraint. <>Not yet, $name. Promise me you’ll come back. Then... then we’ll see where this leads us.<> You nod, understanding the weight of her words and the courage it took her to let you in this much. <>I promise, Gabbie. I’ll come back.<> With one last, lingering look, she steps back, releasing you as you head toward your ship. You cast a final glance over your shoulder, taking in the sight of her standing in the docking bay, watching you with a hopeful yet resolute expression. As you board your now-fixed ship, the hum of the engines feels like a heartbeat, steadying you for the mission ahead. You know this journey carries its dangers, but there’s a newfound sense of purpose fueling you—one that goes beyond finding your father. Now, you’re not only fighting for family but for the promise of something more, something waiting for you to return. <> <>

passages.name: Day5_Takeoff
passages.source_raw:
<>You settle into the pilot’s seat, hands running over the ship’s familiar controls. The hum of the engines resonates through the cabin, a sound you’ve missed more than you realized. Outside the viewport, the station floats in the darkness of space, illuminated only by distant stars and the faint glow of its own lights.
As you prepare for takeoff, memories of the past days flash through your mind—Gabbie’s resilience, Skylar’s easy laughter, Angel’s teasing smile, and the quiet strength of your $mom and $sis. A sense of gratitude fills you; these people, in their own way, helped you hold on to hope and keep fighting. <>I won’t forget this place... or the people I met here, and I have to come back soon. But the mission has to continue.<> You exhale, refocusing on the task at hand. Pulling up the hyperjump module, you enter the coordinates your father had sent—the same coordinates that led you here in the first place, when the hyperdrive malfunctioned and stranded you at the station. With everything repaired, there’s a nervous thrill as you press the final sequence, hoping this time, the ship will hold together. <>Alright, let’s do this. Dad... I’m coming for you.<> As the ship detaches from the docking bay, you watch the station grow smaller and smaller through the viewport. A bittersweet feeling settles over you—this station has been a refuge and a turning point. You know things are waiting for you back here, things you’ll return to. But for now, the journey must go on. With one last look at the station, you initiate the hyperjump sequence, the coordinates locking into place. The engines rev, vibrating the ship as it powers up, and then, with a flash of light, the stars around you blur. The ship lurches forward as it enters hyperspace, propelled toward the unknown. <>This is it. Whatever’s waiting at those coordinates, I’ll be ready.<> In the swirling blue-and-white light of hyperspace, you grip the controls, feeling a renewed sense of purpose. There’s no turning back now. The coordinates are locked, the course set. You’re on your way.
<> <>

passages.name: Day5_Arrival
passages.source_raw:
<>As the hyperjump concludes, the stars settle back into their familiar pinpoints against the black canvas of space. But as you glance at your ship’s map, you notice something unsettling—the navigation system fails to recognize your current location. You’re in an uncharted star system, far from any known routes or outposts. <>How far am I from civilization? Where did they take you, Dad?<> You check the ship’s sensors, scanning the planetary system before you. A single large planet catches your eye—its atmosphere is thick, with vibrant blue and green hues swirling across its surface. The scans reveal a hospitable environment: breathable atmosphere, temperate conditions, and signs of abundant life. It’s beautiful, serene, and unexpectedly inviting for a place so hidden.
As you continue to observe, a soft ping sounds from your comms, breaking the silence. The signal’s origin traces back to the planet, leading you to a set of coordinates that appear on your display. Whoever’s on the other end has sent specific instructions—a landing spot. <>Alright... let’s hope this isn’t some kind of trap.<> Adjusting the ship’s course, you initiate the landing sequence, guiding your vessel through the planet’s upper atmosphere. As you descend, the colors intensify—lush, green canopies stretch beneath you, broken up by rivers that weave like silver threads through the landscape. The beauty of the planet is almost distracting, and you find yourself wondering if this hidden paradise is meant to be some kind of refuge or prison. The ship trembles slightly as it breaches the lower atmosphere, steadying as you bring it down toward the designated landing site. The comms ping once more, signaling you’re on course, and you activate the landing thrusters, guiding the ship with precision toward the coordinates. <>I’m here, Dad. Let’s find out why you called me to this place.<> With a final adjustment, the ship’s landing gear touches down smoothly on the soft ground, surrounded by towering trees and the distant shimmer of water. You power down the engines, the silence enveloping you as you sit back, preparing yourself for whatever lies ahead. <> <>

passages.name: Day5_LandingSite
passages.source_raw:
<><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><>Stepping out of the ship, you’re greeted by the sight of an idyllic beach stretching out before you, the waves lapping softly against the shore. The air is warm, filled with the subtle scent of salt and exotic flowers. In the distance stands a sprawling villa, its white walls glistening under the sun, surrounded by lush greenery and several crystal-clear pools that reflect the sky.
Your eyes quickly find a figure standing near the entrance, waving toward you. Your breath catches—it’s your father. He looks well, almost too well, standing there in casual clothing, appearing far more relaxed than you’d ever expected. As he walks closer, he wears an easy smile, his posture calm and assured.
<>$name, my son! It’s… it’s so good to see you again.<> You hesitate, a sense of wariness tightening your chest. This place is beautiful, but something about it feels surreal, almost unsettling. This isn’t the prison you imagined, and your father—he doesn’t look like a man held captive. He looks… happy? Before you can gather your thoughts, he’s already reached you, placing a steady hand on your shoulder and guiding you toward the villa. <>Come on. Let’s get inside, out of this sun. There’s so much I need to explain.<> You nod, barely managing a response. <>Yes. You do.<> Together, you walk up the path leading to the villa. The grandeur of the place is overwhelming—fountains, sprawling gardens, terraces lined with sun loungers. The villa itself is massive, with high ceilings, open rooms, and wide, airy windows that invite the gentle breeze inside. It’s a place fit for royalty, not for a man supposedly held captive by the Federation.
Inside, you follow him through the grand foyer, your footsteps echoing softly on polished marble floors. Everything here feels surreal, and with each step, the weight of the situation presses down on you harder. <>What kind of prison is this? Why does he look so… content here?<> Your father gestures toward a comfortable seating area, inviting you to sit. He settles across from you, leaning forward, his face a mixture of relief and something you can’t quite place. <>I know this must be confusing, son. But believe me, there’s a reason for everything. I didn’t ask you here lightly.<> His words linger, and you realize there are depths to this place, to his situation, that you’re only beginning to understand. You sit quietly, waiting, the questions building in your mind as he prepares to tell you the truth. <> <>

passages.name: Day5_ConversationStart
passages.source_raw:
<>You sit across from your father in the lavish villa, the comfort of the surroundings sharply contrasting with the weight of the questions pressing on your mind. The gentle breeze drifts through open windows, the distant sound of waves providing an almost surreal backdrop to this reunion. <>Welcome to Paradiso, $name. Or as some of us like to call it… the Federation’s “Gilded Cage.”<> You frown, your gaze shifting to the opulent decor surrounding you.
<>Dad… what is this place? You’re actually imprisoned here? It… it doesn’t look like any prison I’ve ever seen.<> He lets out a soft, bitter laugh, his eyes clouded with a mixture of guilt and resignation. <>Yes. Imprisoned, but in a way that most wouldn’t understand. This is where the Federation sends those who know too much, or who’ve done too much damage to ever be allowed back. They call it a “punishment,” but the truth is, they keep us comfortable here… just comfortable enough to make us complacent.<> He gestures toward the villa around you, the extravagance almost stifling in its abundance. <>Look around. Everything you see—luxury, indulgence, even company when we want it—it’s all a part of the Federation’s design. They know that some people can’t be silenced… so they send us here, where they can keep an eye on us without drawing attention.<> You try to absorb this, struggling to reconcile this paradise with the idea of a prison. There’s a gnawing sense of disbelief as you look at him, at the ease in his expression. <>But… why? Why would they send you here? What did you do to end up in a place like this?<> Your father’s gaze drops, his face shadowed by memories he seems reluctant to revisit. <>I made terrible choices, $name. Choices that cost lives, that broke families. In the Federation’s pursuit of power, I was a willing participant. I created weapons, sanctioned inhumane experiments… and I was good at it. Too good. The people I hurt… they were innocent, caught up in the Federation’s ruthless agenda.<> He runs a hand over his face, as though trying to wipe away the images that haunt him. <>They called it research, progress. I told myself that what I was doing was necessary—that it was for the greater good. But it was a lie, and deep down, I knew it. I just… I didn’t stop. I couldn’t.<> The weight of his confession sinks in, and you find yourself recoiling slightly, not from fear, but from a deep sadness and disbelief. <>But you’re still here. They’ve given you… all of this. Why?<> He lets out a humorless chuckle, glancing around at the opulent surroundings. <>This is both a reward and a prison. They know that people like me—we’re dangerous outside these walls. So they give us everything we could want here: comfort, luxury, every desire fulfilled. All so we’ll stay put, growing lazy and forgetful, too pacified to cause trouble.<> He stands and walks over to the window, gazing out at the idyllic scene beyond. For a moment, you see the same restlessness in him that you felt back on the station—the desire for freedom, battling against the lure of security. <>The Federation doesn’t care if we’re miserable or happy here. They just want us… contained. And they know that, eventually, every one of us will settle in, will let the comforts dull the edges of our convictions.<> You stand, trying to piece together the conflicting emotions building inside you. <>You can’t stay here forever, Dad. Don’t you want to come home? Don’t you want to be free?<> His expression hardens, and he turns to face you, his eyes filled with a painful truth. <>Home? I don’t think I know what that means anymore. This… is my home now. The Federation has made sure of that. Even if I escaped, they’d hunt me to the ends of the galaxy. They’d come after you, your $mom, your $sis. It’s better if I stay here.<> The words hit you like a punch, the gravity of his decision sinking in. You want to shout, to shake him, to tell him he’s wrong. But deep down, a part of you knows that he believes every word he’s saying. <>So that’s it? You’re just… giving up? After everything? What about us? What about the family you left behind?<> There’s a flash of pain in his eyes, and he reaches out, resting a hand on your shoulder. <>I’m sorry, $name. I never wanted to leave you. But some mistakes can’t be undone. And if there’s one thing I can do to protect you… it’s to stay here, where the Federation will keep me hidden and forgotten.<> His voice softens, almost pleading. <>You have a life waiting for you out there. A future. Don’t waste it chasing after a ghost. I’m… I’m not the man you remember. And I’m not worth the risk you’d take trying to bring me back.<> You stare at him, the man who was once your hero, now standing before you as a shadow of that person. The beauty of Paradiso feels hollow, an empty paradise built on regret and betrayal. <>No. I’m not leaving you here. We’ll find a way—together.<> He shakes his head, a sad smile tugging at his lips. <>This place is my sentence, $name. But it doesn’t have to be yours. You can go on and make something of yourself. Leave me here, where I belong.<> <>I don’t believe that. Not for a second.<> He sighs, his expression softening as he pulls you into a brief, tight embrace. <>You’re stronger than I was, $name. You always were. Go, and live the life I couldn’t. Take care of your $mom and $sis. Keep them safe. That’s the greatest gift you could give me.<> You pull back, fighting the tears that threaten to spill over, nodding as you take in his words. The man you knew may be gone, but he’s given you one final mission: to carry on. <>If he won’t leave… then maybe he’s right. Maybe I have to let him go.<> Your father notices the conflict in your eyes and places a reassuring hand on your shoulder. <>You’ve had a long journey, $name. Why don’t you stay here for the night? Rest, recover. There’s no need to rush back into the darkness of space just yet.<> You hesitate, but he gives you a gentle smile, one that seems both comforting and sorrowful. <>I’ve already arranged for you to have a place here tonight. Adriana will show you the way.<> At his words, a woman enters the room, elegantly dressed, her demeanor poised yet warm.
<>Hello, young master. Your father told me to prepare a room for you. Please, come with me.<> She gestures for you to follow, and you give your father a final, searching look. He nods encouragingly, so you turn to Adriana, who leads you through the grand corridors of the villa. The architecture is as extravagant as everything else on this planet—vaulted ceilings, walls adorned with art, and large windows overlooking the serene beach. Adriana stops in front of a spacious room with an open terrace, where the gentle sound of waves fills the space. She gives you a soft smile. <> <>

passages.name: Day5_Room
passages.source_raw:
<>You enter the bedroom that Adriana prepared for you.
<>This will be your room for the night, young master. If you need anything, don’t hesitate to call for me.<> <>Thank you, Adriana. And… just $name is fine.<> She nods, giving you a respectful bow before leaving you alone. You step onto the terrace, taking in the serene beauty of the beach below, the orange hues of the setting sun casting a warm glow over everything. Just as you turn back toward the room, Adriana lingers by the door. <>I’ll go retrieve your belongings from the ship, young master. You’ll have everything you need here.<> <>Oh, there’s no need. I can get them myself. Really.<> She gives you a polite but insistent smile.
<>Please, I insist. It’s part of my duty here.<> Her words linger in the air, carrying a weight you can’t quite place. You watch her leave, and a strange feeling settles over you. Who exactly is Adriana? The way she speaks and moves, so controlled and deferential, gives you an odd sense of discomfort. <>Are there people here, in Paradiso, whose sole purpose is to serve… to meet the whims of people the Federation keeps here? Slaves to “satisfy” the needs of the prisoners in this so-called paradise?<> The thought is unsettling, yet as you survey the luxurious surroundings, you realize it’s not so far-fetched. Everything here seems designed to keep the residents complacent, content. It’s a gilded cage, but there are still bars, unseen and silent. You shake off the thought and walk further into the room, feeling the cool marble floor beneath your feet. The suite is beautifully furnished, with an open-air design that lets the breeze flow through. You sit down on the edge of the bed, allowing yourself to relax for a moment, though your mind remains restless. As you look around the room, an unsettling mix of gratitude and suspicion fills you. This is where your father has chosen to stay, and this is the Federation’s way of “punishing” those who know too much. You decide to head back. <> <>

passages.source_raw:
<><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><><>Back to the livingroom you spot your father. He looks well — rested, tanned, nothing like a prisoner. He gives you a tour of the property: your bedroom, his study, the terrace overlooking silver rivers and jungle canopy. He explains the rules — there are none. The Federation supplies everything. No guards, but satellite surveillance covers the planet. Attempting to leave triggers automated defense. He hands you a pouch of credits. <>Here. You'll need these to enjoy the amenities. Consider it... an allowance from a guilty father.<> <>

passages.name: p_sleep
passages.source_raw:
<>You lay in the villa bed. The sheets are silk. The breeze is warm. The ocean sounds like a lullaby written by someone who owns you.
<> <> <> You dream about your mother and sister, alone at the space station. You wonder if they're worried. $name_sis is probably pacing. Your $mom is probably pretending not to worry, which is worse. <> <> There's a quiet knock at your door. Adriana stands in the hallway, barefoot, her hair loose for the first time since you've been here. <>Can I... come in?<> <> <> You dream about the locked cabinet in your father's study. In the dream, you open it and it's full of photographs — faces you don't recognize staring back at you. One of them mouths a word you can't hear. <> You dream about neural pathways and corridors. A woman with cropped hair stands at the end of a hallway, flickering like a bad signal. She says something in a frequency your ears can't reach. <> You dream about screaming. Lab corridors. Your father behind glass, watching. When you wake, your hands are shaking. The data on your drive is worth more than this entire planet. <> You dream about rain. You're standing in it. Someone beside you — olive skin, black hair — lifts her face to the sky and laughs. <> <> <>You dream about your home planet. The parks. The rain. A life that feels like it belonged to someone else. <>You dream about your ship cutting through stars. The hum of the engine. The only sound in the universe that feels like home. <>You dream about nothing. Just warm dark. It's the best sleep you've had in months.<> <> <> <>

passages.name: p_mq33_confrontation
passages.source_raw:
<> <> <> Your father is on the terrace. Sunset. A glass in his hand, the ice half-melted. He looks up when you step outside.



<>Sit down, $name. Have a drink with me.<>
<>I didn't come here for a drink, Dad. I came here for you.<>
He doesn't react right away. He takes a sip. Sets the glass on the stone railing. Looks at the jungle.
<>I know why you came.<>
<>Then come with me. I have a ship on the beach. We leave tonight, we're in hyperspace before anyone notices you're gone.<>
<>No.<>
<>Dad—<>
<>No. Sit down. Listen.<>
You sit. He stays standing. He pulls his collar aside and presses two fingers against the left side of his neck, just below the jaw. There's a small raised bump under the skin — barely visible, the size of a rice grain.


<>Biochip. Subdermal. Every resident on Paradiso has one. The Federation implants them on arrival. It tracks my location, my vitals, my movement patterns. If I leave the planet's atmosphere without authorization, the chip sends a kill signal to Federation Central Command. Every ship in three sectors gets my coordinates within the hour.<>
<>We can remove it.<>
<>It's wired into my carotid artery. Removal triggers a clotting agent. I'd have a stroke before you got the chip out. The Federation designed it that way on purpose — not as punishment. As insurance. They don't want us dead. They want us here. The chip makes sure we stay.<>
He picks up the glass again. Drinks.
<>There's a man named Jasper. He runs a rebel cell. He was your friend, Dad — your colleague. He's the one who gave me the coordinates to find you. He has resources, a base, a crew. If anyone can figure out how to bypass the chip—<>
<>Jasper.<>
He says the name like he's turning over a coin he found in an old coat.
<>Jasper is alive?<>
<>Very alive. Running operations against the Federation across multiple systems. He's been looking for you for years.<>
<>Of course he has. Jasper was always the stubborn one. I was the one who gave up.<>
He sets the glass down. Rubs his neck where the chip is.
<>Even if they could remove it — even if Jasper has some miracle surgeon who can cut a chip out of a man's neck without killing him — the moment I leave this island, the Federation goes to war. Not a search. A war. They will burn through every system between here and your rebel base looking for me. Every person who helped you, every contact, every safe house. They will find your $mom. They will find your $sis. They will find Jasper. And they will make an example out of all of them.<>
<>So that's it? You just stay here forever?<>
<>I stay here so that everyone I care about stays alive. That's the deal I made. That's the deal I keep making every morning when I wake up and choose breakfast on this terrace instead of a body bag in a Federation morgue.<>
The sunset is dying. Orange to purple to something close to black. The silver rivers below catch the last light and then go dark. Your father looks older in this light. Or maybe he just looks his age for the first time.
<>I have to go back, Dad. I have the evidence — the drives, the data from the bunker, your files. Jasper needs them. The rebellion needs them.<>
<>I know. Take it all. Broadcast it. Let the galaxy see what the Federation did and who signed off on it. I don't care anymore. My name is already on those documents — let it be on the news too.<>
<>$mom is going to ask about you. She's going to want to know why I came back without you. She's been waiting for you since the day we left Haven. She hasn't stopped.<>
He's quiet. The glass is empty. The ice is gone.
<>I know she has...<>
<>She needs to hear it from you. Why you're staying. What happened. All of it.<>
<>I will write a letter.<>
He nods slowly. Picks up the empty glass and looks at it like he's looking through it at something a long way behind him.
<>I'll write it tonight. I'll have it for you tomorrow morning. Come to the study.<>
He pauses.

passages.name: p_mq34_letter
passages.source_raw:
<> <> <> Morning. The study. Your father is at his desk, sleeves rolled, hair uncombed. An empty coffee cup and three crumpled pieces of paper in the wastebasket. He looks like he's been here all night.

On the desk: a sealed envelope. Cream-colored, heavy stock. Your $mom's name written on the front in his handwriting.
<>It's done.<>
<>What did you write?<>
<>Enough for her to understand. Enough for her to stop waiting.<>
He picks up the envelope and holds it for a second. Turns it over in his hands. Then he offers it to you.

<>I told her I'm happy here. And I am — that's the worst part, isn't it? I'm more comfortable than I have any right to be. Better fed, better rested, more at peace than I ever was at home. And she needs to know that so she can stop imagining me suffering in some cell. I'm not suffering. I'm having breakfast on a terrace and reading books in the sunshine.<>
You take the envelope.
<>I told her to move on. To take care of you and $name_sis and to do something. Whatever she wants. I told her she's spent enough years looking at the door.<>
<> He opens the desk drawer and pulls out a small data chip. Brushed steel, Federation insignia on the surface.
<>One more thing. My old access codes. Encrypted frequencies, backdoor protocols. The Federation doesn't rotate high-clearance credentials often. Give these to Jasper. He'll know what to do with them.<>
<>Are you sure?<>
<>I used those codes to authorize terrible things for years. Maybe Jasper can use them to undo some of it. Seems fair.<>
<>
@@color:white;OBTAINED: Federation Access Codes@@
He stands. Puts his hands in his pockets. Looks at you the way you look at something you're about to lose and have already accepted losing.
<>Take care of your $mom. Take care of $name_sis. And tell Jasper he was right about everything. He'll appreciate hearing that from me — even secondhand.<>
<>I will.<>
<>Good. Now go before I start talking more and ruin it.<>
<> <> <> <>

passages.name: p_mq30_bunker
passages.source_raw:
<> <> The garden at the south wall. Thick vines covering the stone, bougainvillea growing wild over a section nobody maintains. Adriana crouches and pulls the foliage aside. A rusted metal grate, bolted from the inside — she reaches through and pops the latch with practiced fingers.

<>I oiled these hinges when I was fourteen. They still work.<>
You descend a metal ladder into darkness. Emergency lights flicker on — dim red strips along the floor. The air drops ten degrees. Cool, dry, humming with electronics. The smell of ozone and dust.

The tunnel runs straight for about thirty meters, pipes and cable bundles along the ceiling. Then it opens up.


Rows of servers. Floor to ceiling, black metal, blinking indicator lights in blue and green. Six screens on the far wall showing live feeds — the terrace, the bar, the lagoon, the library, the bedrooms. Every villa. Every room. Your father sitting at his desk reading. Crowell asleep on a bar stool. Kailani adjusting a buoy in the lagoon. All of it. Live. Recorded. Stored.
<>They see everything.<>
<>Everything. Audio too. See that?<>
She points at a screen showing a directory structure — folders labelled by date, stretching back years. Communication logs, tagged and timestamped, between addresses labelled FC-CENTRAL and PARADISO-ADMIN.
<>Orders for resident transfers. Supply manifests. Behavioral reports. And this—<>
She pulls up a subdirectory. The header reads PROJECT ECHO — FULL EXPERIMENTAL DATABASE.
<>This is what we found in the cabinet but a hundred times over. Raw footage, raw data, unredacted. Your father's cabinet had the report. This is the source material.<>
You plug your drive into the main terminal. A progress bar appears. Twenty percent. Forty. The servers hum louder. The lights on the racks flicker in sequence like a heartbeat.


<>How long?<>
<>Few minutes. The files are big.<>
You wait. The red emergency lights make everything look like a photograph of a crime scene. Adriana stands beside you, arms crossed, watching the progress bar. Seventy percent. Eighty.
<>My mother knew about this room. She told me about it near the end, when she was too sick to come down here herself. She said if anyone ever came to this island who could actually do something with what's stored here, I should show them.<>
<>She was waiting for someone like me?<>
<>She was waiting for anyone. You just happened to be the one who showed up.<>
One hundred percent. The progress bar fills. You pull the drive.
<>Got it. Everything.<>
You turn to leave. Adriana is standing in the corridor. She's shaking — hands, shoulders, a fine tremor running through her. Adrenaline working its way out. She looks at you in the red light.
She steps forward and kisses you. Hard. Her hands grip the front of your shirt and she pulls herself into you. She tastes like adrenaline and the blue drink from last night and something underneath both — something warm and desperate and real.
You kiss her back. Your hand finds the back of her neck. The hum of the servers fills the silence between breaths.
She pulls away. Forehead against your chin. Still shaking.
<>Take me with you. When you leave this island. I don't care where.<>
<>Adriana—<>
<>Don't answer yet. Just... I don't want to be alone after this. Can I sleep with you tonight?.<>
<> <> <> <>
@@color:pink;Adriana relationship increased.@@
@@color:white;Adriana will come to your room tonight.@@
<> <> <>

passages.name: p_mq28_residents
passages.source_raw:
<> <> <> Your father walks you down the cliff path to the Jungle Bar. The late afternoon light turns the bamboo columns amber. Low music drifts from somewhere — an old recording, something with strings. Half a dozen people are scattered across the bar in various states of expensive decay.



<>These are the residents. The ones who come out, at least. Some haven't left their villas in months. These are the social ones — which, on Paradiso, means they still bother putting on pants.<>
He steers you toward a ruddy-faced man at the bar who's already waving you over. Thick neck, burst capillaries across his nose, a steel dive watch on a wrist as wide as your forearm. He shakes your hand before you offer it — hard, the grip of a man who used to command and now just squeezes things.


<>So this is the kid! I've heard about you. Your old man talks about you when he's had enough whiskey — which, let's be honest, is most evenings. Crowell. Ex-Admiral. Ex-everything, really. Sit down, have a drink.<>
<>He's not drinking, Crowell.<>
<>Not yet. Give him a week.<>
He laughs at his own joke. Nobody else does.

<> <>
Your father guides you to a quieter corner where an elderly man in a cream linen suit is reading from a leather-bound notebook, a pen tucked behind his ear. He looks up as you approach — clear dark eyes, white hair combed neatly back, the measured posture of someone who's been sitting in chairs and thinking for sixty years.


<>$name, this is Dr. Fen Hashimoto. Biologist. Probably the smartest person on this island, which he'll deny and then prove in the next sentence.<>
<>Your father flatters me because I'm old and he thinks old people need flattering. You must be the visitor everyone's been whispering about. Welcome.<>
He closes his notebook and gives you his full attention. The kind of man who does that — who stops what he's doing and actually looks at you.

<> <>
Your father orders two drinks — one for himself, one he sets in front of you without asking if you want it. You both look out over the jungle canopy. The light is shifting — gold bleeding toward orange.
<>There's one more person you should know about.<>
He nods toward the far end of the bar. A woman sits alone on the last stool, her back slightly turned to the room. Cropped auburn hair, black tank top, a tattoo running from behind her left ear down her neck to her collarbone — fine lines, technical, like a circuit diagram printed on skin. She's nursing a whiskey and watching the jungle like she's expecting it to do something.


<>Nyx. She's been here longer than most. Keeps to herself. Doesn't talk to anyone, doesn't join anything, doesn't attend the dinners I sometimes host. Just drinks and reads and disappears. I've tried to reach her a few times over the years. She's not interested.<>
<>What's her deal?<>
<>Nobody knows the full story. Something scientific — she was a researcher of some kind. The Federation put her here and she stopped talking about why a long time ago.<>
You glance at her again. She looks up — not at your father, at you. Grey-green eyes, direct, unflinching. The kind of look that takes your measure in two seconds and files it. She holds it for a beat. Then she turns back to her whiskey.
Your father raises his glass in her direction — a small gesture, habitual, probably something he does every evening. She doesn't acknowledge it.

<>Don't take it personally. She's like that with everyone. I think she prefers it.<>
<> <> <> <>

passages.name: p_kailani_nightswim
passages.source_raw:
<> <> <> The lagoon is transformed. Bioluminescent organisms pulse beneath the surface — electric blue, shifting in slow waves with the current. The beach is empty. The stars are thick overhead, more than you've ever seen in one sky. The air smells like warm salt and night-blooming flowers.

Kailani is already in the water, waist-deep. Her skin is painted in blue light from below. Her hair fans out behind her on the surface, black against the glow. The gold pendant from her grandmother catches a point of light at her throat.

<>You came.<>
<>You asked.<>
<>I ask a lot of things. People don't usually show up.<>
You wade in. The water is warm — warmer than during the day somehow. The bioluminescence wraps around your legs as you move, trails of blue following every step. You stop next to her. The glow lights you both from below — silver and blue, like standing inside a nebula.
<>I come here every night. After the residents go to sleep, after the bar closes, after the island goes quiet. This is the only hour that belongs to me.<>
She tilts her head back and looks at the stars. The water laps at her collarbone.
<>The Federation engineered everything on this planet. The birds, the fruit trees, the coral, the sunsets — all manufactured. Hashimoto told me they even seed new insect species every quarter to keep the ecosystem running. But this —<>
She runs her hand through the water. Blue light trails from her fingers like liquid electricity.
<>— this is natural. The bioluminescence was here before the Federation. Before the villas, before the landing pads, before any of it. It's the one thing they didn't fake. The one thing on this island that's real.<>
You float side by side. The sky above, the glow below. Silence for a while — the good kind, where neither of you needs to fill it.
<>Why did you really stay, Kailani? Two years is a long time for a paycheck.<>
She's quiet for a moment. When she speaks, her voice is lower.
<>At first it was the money. Then it was fear — I didn't have a plan for what came after. And then it was... I don't know. Inertia. You spend long enough somewhere, even somewhere like this, and it starts to feel like the only place that exists. The rest of the galaxy becomes an idea instead of a real thing. You tell yourself 'one more month' and then one more month turns into one more year and then you stop counting.<>
<>That sounds familiar.<>
<>Your father said the same thing to me once. First year I was here. He said 'Kailani, this island makes you forget there's an outside.' I thought he was being dramatic but he wasn't.<>
The waves push you closer together. Her shoulder brushes yours underwater.
<>But then you showed up. And suddenly there's someone who comes from out there. Someone with a ship and a reason and mud on his boots from other planets. And it reminds me that the galaxy is real and I'm wasting myself on a beach that doesn't even belong to me.<>
She turns to face you. The bioluminescence lights her from below — her jaw, her cheekbones, the gold pendant, the gold ring in her irises.
<>Thank you, $name. For the locker. For coming here tonight. For reminding me that I used to want things.<>
She leans in and kisses you. Slow, warm, her wet hand on the side of your face. She tastes like salt water and something sweet. The glow pulses around you both — brighter for a second, like even the ocean noticed.
She pulls back. Smiles — not the big open grin from the beach. Something quieter. Just for you.
<>Come find me tomorrow. At the lagoon. During the day. I have the afternoon off and I want to spend it with you. Not working. Not running activities. Just... us.<>
<>I'll be there.<>
<>Promise?<>
<>Promise.<>
She swims backward, the glow trailing from her body like a comet's tail. She waves once from the shallows, wrings out her hair, and walks barefoot up the sand toward her quarters. The pendant glints once in the starlight. Then she's gone.
You float alone for a while. The lagoon glows. The stars turn. The water holds you.
<>
@@color:pink;Kailani relationship increased.@@
@@color:white;Find Kailani at the lagoon tomorrow.@@
<> <> <>

passages.name: p_kailani_meet
passages.source_raw:
<> <> <> A tall Polynesian woman is crouched by the water's edge, adjusting a buoy marker. Long black hair loose past her shoulders, bikini, swimmer's build. She stands and spots you — waves you over without hesitation, like she's been expecting company for two years and you're the first person who showed up.


<>Hey! You're new. I know everyone on this island and I've never seen your face before. I'm Kailani.<>
<>$name. I'm... staying with my father at the main villa.<>
<>Ah — you're his kid. I heard someone landed a ship on the beach pad. Everyone here talked about it for a full day. That's how starved for news this place is.<>
She smiles — warm, open, no guard behind it. Gold ring around her dark irises catching the sun.
<>You don't seem like the other residents.<>
<>That's because I'm not. I'm staff — hired by the Federation to run recreation for the residents. Swimming, beach activities, that kind of thing. I actually chose to come here. For the money.<>
<>You chose this?<>
<>The Federation pays incredibly well for people willing to live on a planet that doesn't officially exist. I figured I'd stay a year, save up enough to buy my own ship, and leave. That was two years ago.<>
She picks up a volleyball from the sand and tosses it hand to hand.
<>You look like you could use some fresh air. What do you want to do?<>
<> <> <><> <> <><> <> <>

passages.name: p_kailani_favor
passages.source_raw:
<> <> <> Kailani is pacing near the equipment shed. She's not setting up activities, not swimming, not smiling. Her arms are crossed and her jaw is tight. She sees you and her expression shifts — relief mixed with something she doesn't want to show.


<>$name. Hey. Can I— can I ask you something? It's stupid. It's not stupid. It's embarrassing.<>
<>What happened?<>
She uncrosses her arms. Crosses them again.
<>There's a storage locker behind the equipment shed where I keep my personal things. My communicator, some credits I've been saving, a necklace my grandmother gave me before I left home. It's all I have that's actually mine on this island.<>
She looks toward the bar on the cliff.
<>Crowell — the admiral — he came down here three days ago, hammered as usual. He said he needed to borrow the it for something. I told him no. He broke the lock and took the whole locker. Said he'd give it back when he was done. That was three days ago. He won't return my messages and he's always surrounded by drinking buddies at the bar.<>
<>He stole your stuff?<>
<>He'd call it 'borrowing.' Everyone here does whatever they want because there are no rules and no consequences. The Federation doesn't care if residents harass the staff. We're not people to them — we're part of the furniture. Like the volleyball net.<>
Her voice is steady but her hands are shaking. This isn't just about a locker. It's about two years of being invisible.
<>I can't go up there myself. He's a retired admiral who outweighs me by sixty pounds and thinks the island belongs to him. But you — you're a resident's son. He'd listen to you. Maybe.<>
<>I'll handle it. Where does he hang out?<>
<>The Jungle Bar. Always. He's got my locker behind the counter — asked the bartender to store it for him. Just... get it back? Please?<>
<> <> <>

passages.name: p_lagoon_swim
passages.source_raw:
<> <> <> <> <>You strip down and wade into the lagoon. The water is absurdly clear — turquoise over white sand, coral formations visible twenty feet below. You swim hard, arms cutting the surface, lungs burning in the good way. A school of silver fish scatters beneath you like shrapnel. <>The water hits your skin and every muscle in your body unclenches at once. You push off the sand bottom and glide, face down, watching the coral pass beneath you in slow motion. A ray drifts by — flat, dark, unbothered by your existence. You swim until your shoulders ache. <>You dive in headfirst and the silence swallows you. Underwater, the lagoon is another world — blue light, slow movement, the muffled thud of your own heartbeat. You surface gasping and swim laps along the shoreline until your arms feel like rope. <>The lagoon is empty this morning. Just you and the water and the sound of your own breathing. You swim hard — freestyle, no pacing, burning through it like you're trying to outrun something. By the time you stop, you're fifty meters from shore and your chest is heaving. <>You wade in waist-deep and float on your back. The sky above is painfully blue. You close your eyes and let the salt hold you. Then you flip and swim — hard, angry almost, each stroke a punch at the water. It doesn't fight back. It never does. That's the problem with paradise. <>A warm current catches you as you wade in — the lagoon is warmer today, almost bathwater. You swim lazy laps, dipping below the surface to watch the coral shift colour in the light. A sea turtle glides past at arm's length, ancient and indifferent. You swim until the tension in your neck finally lets go. <>


<>
@@color:#e8c320;STR +2@@

<> <> <>
